name: CI
display_title: Make the HloModule metadata accessors of Executable virtual

head_commit.message:
Make the HloModule metadata accessors of Executable virtual

`Executable` owns the `HloModule` it was compiled from and reads all module
metadata from it. We want backends to be able to keep the module themselves (or
not at all), and `GpuExecutable` in particular shouldn't need the module to
answer simple questions like "what's the aliasing of the entry computation".

So this change makes `shared_module()` and `module_config()` virtual and adds
virtual `input_output_alias_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()`. `module()`
and `has_module()` stay non-virtual and go through a new protected virtual
`module_ptr()`, so that subclasses that keep their own module only have to
override `shared_module()` and `module_ptr()`. All defaults read the module the
base class holds, so nothing changes for any backend.

I also removed `execution_count_`, which nothing used anymore.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019995882

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Check select predicate replication in WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check select predicate replication in WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion

`IsAllReduceMovable` in `WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion` allowed `kSelect` between
a collective result and zero without checking whether the predicate is
replicated across each reduction group. Similarly, the `kMultiply` scaling
pattern did not verify that the broadcasted scalar `all-reduce` factor is
replicated within each group of the gradient `all-reduce`. When a while loop
masks or scales an `all-reduce` or `reduce-scatter` output with a value that
varies within the reduction group before accumulating, sinking the collective
out of the loop produces wrong per device sums.

Require `is_value_replicated_within_replica_group` on both the `kSelect`
predicate and the `kMultiply` scaling factor. For `kReduceScatter`, also
restrict `kSelect` to direct collective users whose users are all `kAdd`, and
disallow `kConvert` and `kBroadcast` users so
`ChangeAccumulatorShapesInLoopBodies` only rewrites supported shapes. Existing
programs with replicated predicates and matching reduction groups do not change.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025565492

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

A call annotated with _xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>" is
wrapped into an async region by ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper and
assigned LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>) by ExecutionStreamAssignment, so it
runs on that domain's stream. The wrapper rejects locality-domain regions
that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and
AsyncStartThunk::Prepare rejects communication thunks inside them at
runtime. Stream annotations are kept only on the call, not on the
get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.

head_commit.message:
PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52821

📝 Summary of Changes

Lets an XLA program run a computation on a chosen locality domain by annotating a call with `_xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>"`. Builds on the stream building blocks ([#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124)) and their execution support ([#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302)).
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper`: wraps a locality-domain-annotated call into an async region. It rejects regions that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and annotations that aren't on a non-inlineable call.
- `ExecutionStreamAssignment`: assigns `LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>)` to those regions, without using up a round-robin compute stream.
- `AsyncStartThunk::Prepare`: rejects communication thunks inside a locality-domain region at runtime.
- **MHLO → HLO**: stream annotations stay on the call, not on the get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.
- `side_effect_util`: adds `kXlaLocalityDomainStreamAnnotationPrefix` (`"locality_domain:"`).

🎯 Justification

This is the first PR that lets a program annotate calls to run on a locality domain's stream, using the runtime support from [#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302). Programs without these annotations are unchanged.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this enables locality-domain execution

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `ExecutionStreamAssignmentTest`:
  - `ValidLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.AssignsLocalityDomainStream`;
  - `MalformedLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.DiesWithCheckMessage`;
  - `LocalityDomainAnnotationRejectsCommunicationScope`;
  - `LocalityDomainDoesNotConsumeRoundRobinStream`.
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapperTest` (10 tests):
  - wrapping a call while keeping its attributes; idempotence; tuple calls with get-tuple-element users;
  - rejecting missing or inlineable calls, transitive collectives, nested annotations and send/recv;
  - returning an error status inside fusions and async computations.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainPrepareRejectsCommunicationThunks`: a compute-only region prepares successfully, and one containing a communication thunk is rejected.
- `frontend_attributes.mlir`: stream annotations aren't copied onto the get-tuple-elements of a multi-result call.

🧪 Execution Tests:

`LocalityDomainComputeTest` runs on a single GPU, and skips on GPUs with fewer than two locality domains.
- `AnnotatedCallsBecomeLocalityDomainRegions`: two dependent calls annotated `locality_domain:0` and `locality_domain:1` become async regions on their domains in the optimized module.
- `AnnotatedCallsProduceCorrectResults`: the same program matches the interpreter's results.

display_title: [XLA] Check select predicate replication in WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check select predicate replication in WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion

`IsAllReduceMovable` in `WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion` allowed `kSelect` between
a collective result and zero without checking whether the predicate is
replicated across each reduction group. Similarly, the `kMultiply` scaling
pattern did not verify that the broadcasted scalar `all-reduce` factor is
replicated within each group of the gradient `all-reduce`. When a while loop
masks or scales an `all-reduce` or `reduce-scatter` output with a value that
varies within the reduction group before accumulating, sinking the collective
out of the loop produces wrong per device sums.

Require `is_value_replicated_within_replica_group` on both the `kSelect`
predicate and the `kMultiply` scaling factor. For `kReduceScatter`, also
restrict `kSelect` to direct collective users whose users are all `kAdd`, and
disallow `kConvert` and `kBroadcast` users so
`ChangeAccumulatorShapesInLoopBodies` only rewrites supported shapes. Existing
programs with replicated predicates and matching reduction groups do not change.

display_title: [XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

📝 Summary of Changes

PR #52906 restricted HandleMaximum's maximum(a, clamp(a, x, b)) -> clamp(a, x, b) rewrite using IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (via HloEvaluator and ComparisonDirection::kLe).
That still leaves several issues:
- +0.0 <= -0.0 evaluates to true under partial order, folding max(+0.0, clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0)) to clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0) (-0.0 instead of +0.0).
- Building a kLt/kLe kCompare and calling HloEvaluator::Evaluate aborts AlgebraicSimplifier::Run() with UnimplementedError on complex bounds (c64/c128) and TF_RET_CHECK-fails on mixed-FP bounds (both in HandleMaximum and in MinMaxToClamp).
- IsKnownLessThanOrEqual folds lhs == rhs unconditionally and allocates a fresh HloEvaluator on every match.

This change replaces IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (and HloEvaluator in MinMaxToClamp) with a shared CompareConstantBounds helper that checks matching, non-complex array element types and evaluates strict lower < upper directly on the scalar literals via PrimitiveTypeSwitch and Comparison, removing the hlo_evaluator dependency from algebraic_simplifier. Degenerate equal-bound clamps (a == b) are not worth special-casing, matching MinMaxToClamp.

🎯 Justification

Follow-up to #52659 / #52906: prevents sign-bit flips on (+0.0, -0.0) clamp bounds, prevents AlgebraicSimplifier pass failures on complex or mixed-precision bounds, and avoids HloEvaluator overhead during simplification.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier_test.cc:
- MaxOfClamp: ordered constant bounds (0 and 6); expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithBroadcastBounds: broadcast ordered bounds with maximum operands swapped; expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithUnorderedBounds: constant bounds 10 and 0; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithParameterBounds: runtime parameter bounds; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithSignedZeroBounds: constant bounds +0.0 and -0.0; expects no change (fails with a <= check).
- MaxOfClampWithComplexBounds: c64 constant bounds; expects no change without failing.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added.

head_commit.message:
PR #46000: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Backend selection and fusion wiring (PR 6/8)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the 6th in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995
PR 2/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45996
PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997
PR 4/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45998
PR 5/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999
PR 6/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000   <---- This PR
PR 7/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001
PR 8/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46002

This PR adds the xla_gpu_experimental_triton_ragged_dot flag (defaults to false) and wire up the Triton/XTile path in GemmRewriterVisitor::HandleRaggedDot().

When the flag is enabled:
- IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() validates the ragged-dot for Triton.
- A Triton/XTile fusion is created with default tile sizes.
- The existing cuDNN (CUDA) and hipBLASLt (ROCm) paths are unchanged
  and remain the default.

Also adds backend_configs.proto field for ragged-dot tile config.

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

2f4fb58c408800e5f60ba09f72af33810ba7e0eb by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Unify ragged-dot backend selection and wire up the XTile fusion

Add the xla_gpu_experimental_triton_ragged_dot flag (false by default) and
route every ragged-dot through a single function, SelectRaggedDotBackend(),
in xla/service/gpu/ir_emission_utils -- the shared utility both passes
already depend on.  It applies the priority order once:

  1a. cuDNN        - IsCudnnSupportedRaggedDot()
  1b. hipBLASLt    - IsGpublasLtSupportedGroupedMatMul()
  2.  Triton XTile - IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot()
  3.  default      - expand into a regular dot

CanBeHandledByCuDNNFusion() and CanBeHandledByGpublasltGroupGemm() moved to
ir_emission_utils as the two Is*Supported* helpers above; HandleRaggedDot()
is split into RewriteRaggedDotAsGroupedGemmCustomCall() and
RewriteRaggedDotAsTritonFusion().  When the flag is on and no higher-priority
backend claims the instruction, a kTritonFusionKind fusion is emitted with
default tile sizes.  The cuDNN and hipBLASLt paths are unchanged.

IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() restricts the XTile path to what the emitter
handles: Ampere+ on NVIDIA, one contracting and one non-contracting dimension
per side, a leading flat batch prefix, a group_sizes shape matching the
ragged mode, matching operand types apart from the mixed-FP8 pairs, and a
signed-integer group_sizes operand.

--
3ddb4fca2d5dc97f0fb0b955f0d9461757afbe93 by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Let a refused cuDNN probe fall through to another backend

SelectRaggedDotBackend() returned a single choice, so a ragged-dot that
passed the static cuDNN gates but that cuDNN had no execution plan for was
expanded into a dense dot even when the Triton XTile or gpuBLASLt path could
have taken it.

It becomes SelectRaggedDotBackends(), returning the eligible backends in
priority order; an empty result is what RaggedDotRewriter expands, so the
kDefault enumerator is gone.  Callers drop a leading kCuDnn when the cuDNN
probe refuses the ragged-dot and fall through to the next candidate.

RaggedDotRewriter and GemmRewriter must agree on the head of the list, so
GemmRewriter takes the same is_supported_by_cudnn_fusion callback, passed
from AddGemmRewriterPasses.  It only probes when the list holds a candidate
behind kCuDnn: with kCuDnn alone there is nothing to rewrite either way, and
RaggedDotRewriter has already expanded the ragged-dot if cuDNN refused it.
The autotuner pipelines are unchanged; they pass the default cudnn_version,
which keeps kCuDnn out of the list.

display_title: PR #46000: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Backend selection and fusion wiring (PR 6/8)

head_commit.message:
PR #46000: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Backend selection and fusion wiring (PR 6/8)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the 6th in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995
PR 2/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45996
PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997
PR 4/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45998
PR 5/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999
PR 6/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000   <---- This PR
PR 7/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001
PR 8/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46002

This PR adds the xla_gpu_experimental_triton_ragged_dot flag (defaults to false) and wire up the Triton/XTile path in GemmRewriterVisitor::HandleRaggedDot().

When the flag is enabled:
- IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() validates the ragged-dot for Triton.
- A Triton/XTile fusion is created with default tile sizes.
- The existing cuDNN (CUDA) and hipBLASLt (ROCm) paths are unchanged
  and remain the default.

Also adds backend_configs.proto field for ragged-dot tile config.

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply:⚡️ Performance Improvement, ✨ New Feature

2f4fb58c408800e5f60ba09f72af33810ba7e0eb by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Unify ragged-dot backend selection and wire up the XTile fusion

Add the xla_gpu_experimental_triton_ragged_dot flag (false by default) and
route every ragged-dot through a single function, SelectRaggedDotBackend(),
in xla/service/gpu/ir_emission_utils -- the shared utility both passes
already depend on.  It applies the priority order once:

  1a. cuDNN        - IsCudnnSupportedRaggedDot()
  1b. hipBLASLt    - IsGpublasLtSupportedGroupedMatMul()
  2.  Triton XTile - IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot()
  3.  default      - expand into a regular dot

CanBeHandledByCuDNNFusion() and CanBeHandledByGpublasltGroupGemm() moved to
ir_emission_utils as the two Is*Supported* helpers above; HandleRaggedDot()
is split into RewriteRaggedDotAsGroupedGemmCustomCall() and
RewriteRaggedDotAsTritonFusion().  When the flag is on and no higher-priority
backend claims the instruction, a kTritonFusionKind fusion is emitted with
default tile sizes.  The cuDNN and hipBLASLt paths are unchanged.

IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() restricts the XTile path to what the emitter
handles: Ampere+ on NVIDIA, one contracting and one non-contracting dimension
per side, a leading flat batch prefix, a group_sizes shape matching the
ragged mode, matching operand types apart from the mixed-FP8 pairs, and a
signed-integer group_sizes operand.

--
3ddb4fca2d5dc97f0fb0b955f0d9461757afbe93 by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Let a refused cuDNN probe fall through to another backend

SelectRaggedDotBackend() returned a single choice, so a ragged-dot that
passed the static cuDNN gates but that cuDNN had no execution plan for was
expanded into a dense dot even when the Triton XTile or gpuBLASLt path could
have taken it.

It becomes SelectRaggedDotBackends(), returning the eligible backends in
priority order; an empty result is what RaggedDotRewriter expands, so the
kDefault enumerator is gone.  Callers drop a leading kCuDnn when the cuDNN
probe refuses the ragged-dot and fall through to the next candidate.

RaggedDotRewriter and GemmRewriter must agree on the head of the list, so
GemmRewriter takes the same is_supported_by_cudnn_fusion callback, passed
from AddGemmRewriterPasses.  It only probes when the list holds a candidate
behind kCuDnn: with kCuDnn alone there is nothing to rewrite either way, and
RaggedDotRewriter has already expanded the ragged-dot if cuDNN refused it.
The autotuner pipelines are unchanged; they pass the default cudnn_version,
which keeps kCuDnn out of the list.

display_title: [XLA] Check select predicate replication in WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check select predicate replication in WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion

`IsAllReduceMovable` in `WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion` allowed `kSelect` between
a collective result and zero without checking whether the predicate is
replicated across each reduction group. Similarly, the `kMultiply` scaling
pattern did not verify that the broadcasted scalar `all-reduce` factor is
replicated within each group of the gradient `all-reduce`. When a while loop
masks or scales an `all-reduce` or `reduce-scatter` output with a value that
varies within the reduction group before accumulating, sinking the collective
out of the loop produces wrong per device sums.

Require `is_value_replicated_within_replica_group` on both the `kSelect`
predicate and the `kMultiply` scaling factor. For `kReduceScatter`, also
restrict `kSelect` to direct collective users whose users are all `kAdd`, and
disallow `kConvert` and `kBroadcast` users so
`ChangeAccumulatorShapesInLoopBodies` only rewrites supported shapes. Existing
programs with replicated predicates and matching reduction groups do not change.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Lower expm1 and log1p directly to TensorIR ops.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Lower expm1 and log1p directly to TensorIR ops.

Decomposing `expm1(x)` into `exp(x) - 1` and `log1p(x)` into `log(x + 1)` loses precision for inputs near zero. Map `stablehlo.exponential_minus_one` and `stablehlo.log_plus_one` directly to `nv_tensor_ir.expm1` and `nv_tensor_ir.log1p` (added in `tensor-ir` v0.1.8), and remove `CreateFloatSplat` along with the manual decompositions.

display_title: [XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

📝 Summary of Changes

PR #52906 restricted HandleMaximum's maximum(a, clamp(a, x, b)) -> clamp(a, x, b) rewrite using IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (via HloEvaluator and ComparisonDirection::kLe).
That still leaves several issues:
- +0.0 <= -0.0 evaluates to true under partial order, folding max(+0.0, clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0)) to clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0) (-0.0 instead of +0.0).
- Building a kLt/kLe kCompare and calling HloEvaluator::Evaluate aborts AlgebraicSimplifier::Run() with UnimplementedError on complex bounds (c64/c128) and TF_RET_CHECK-fails on mixed-FP bounds (both in HandleMaximum and in MinMaxToClamp).
- IsKnownLessThanOrEqual folds lhs == rhs unconditionally and allocates a fresh HloEvaluator on every match.

This change replaces IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (and HloEvaluator in MinMaxToClamp) with a shared CompareConstantBounds helper that checks matching, non-complex array element types and evaluates strict lower < upper directly on the scalar literals via PrimitiveTypeSwitch and Comparison, removing the hlo_evaluator dependency from algebraic_simplifier. Degenerate equal-bound clamps (a == b) are not worth special-casing, matching MinMaxToClamp.

🎯 Justification

Follow-up to #52659 / #52906: prevents sign-bit flips on (+0.0, -0.0) clamp bounds, prevents AlgebraicSimplifier pass failures on complex or mixed-precision bounds, and avoids HloEvaluator overhead during simplification.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier_test.cc:
- MaxOfClamp: ordered constant bounds (0 and 6); expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithBroadcastBounds: broadcast ordered bounds with maximum operands swapped; expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithUnorderedBounds: constant bounds 10 and 0; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithParameterBounds: runtime parameter bounds; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithSignedZeroBounds: constant bounds +0.0 and -0.0; expects no change (fails with a <= check).
- MaxOfClampWithComplexBounds: c64 constant bounds; expects no change without failing.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU][TensorIR] Add variadic reduce support through reduce_ud

The StableHLO legalization (ReduceOpConversion) now accepts
reductions with many inputs and results. It lowers them to
nv_tensor_ir.reduce_ud. support.cc now allows tuple-shaped
reduce results, and a new reduce_ud.hlo test checks a
(value, index) argmax-style reduction. Before this change,
only single-input reductions worked, so argmax-style fusions
could not use the TensorIR backend.

name: CI
display_title: Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

head_commit.message:
Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Reusing these buffers as well lowers the peak memory, but a reused buffer stays at the same offset for longer, which can increase the fragmentation by more than the reuse saves. So always reusing them makes some modules smaller and others larger.

Therefore this change adds `HeapSimulator::RunWithBeneficialOperandReuse`, which `BufferAssigner` now uses. If a heap simulation reused such a buffer, the allocs and frees are replayed without this kind of reuse (new `HeapSimulator::Options::may_reuse_operand_buffers_through_other_positions`), and the reuse is only kept if it results in a smaller heap.

Comparing the heaps needs a second `HeapAlgorithm::Finish()`, which is slow on large modules for the `kSpatial` and `kTemporal` packing strategies. So for algorithms without a fast `Finish()` (new `HeapAlgorithm::HasFastFinish()`), the reuse is dropped right away if it does not lower the peak memory. Stats-only runs (`NoFragmentationStatsHeap` in `MinimumMemoryForModule`) stay restricted to direct operands so schedule scoring in `DefaultMemoryScheduler` does not change.

head_commit.message:
PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52821

📝 Summary of Changes

Lets an XLA program run a computation on a chosen locality domain by annotating a call with `_xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>"`. Builds on the stream building blocks ([#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124)) and their execution support ([#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302)).
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper`: wraps a locality-domain-annotated call into an async region. It rejects regions that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and annotations that aren't on a non-inlineable call.
- `ExecutionStreamAssignment`: assigns `LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>)` to those regions, without using up a round-robin compute stream.
- `AsyncStartThunk::Prepare`: rejects communication thunks inside a locality-domain region at runtime.
- **MHLO → HLO**: stream annotations stay on the call, not on the get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.
- `side_effect_util`: adds `kXlaLocalityDomainStreamAnnotationPrefix` (`"locality_domain:"`).

🎯 Justification

This is the first PR that lets a program annotate calls to run on a locality domain's stream, using the runtime support from [#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302). Programs without these annotations are unchanged.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this enables locality-domain execution

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `ExecutionStreamAssignmentTest`:
  - `ValidLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.AssignsLocalityDomainStream`;
  - `MalformedLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.DiesWithCheckMessage`;
  - `LocalityDomainAnnotationRejectsCommunicationScope`;
  - `LocalityDomainDoesNotConsumeRoundRobinStream`.
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapperTest` (10 tests):
  - wrapping a call while keeping its attributes; idempotence; tuple calls with get-tuple-element users;
  - rejecting missing or inlineable calls, transitive collectives, nested annotations and send/recv;
  - returning an error status inside fusions and async computations.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainPrepareRejectsCommunicationThunks`: a compute-only region prepares successfully, and one containing a communication thunk is rejected.
- `frontend_attributes.mlir`: stream annotations aren't copied onto the get-tuple-elements of a multi-result call.

🧪 Execution Tests:

`LocalityDomainComputeTest` runs on a single GPU, and skips on GPUs with fewer than two locality domains.
- `AnnotatedCallsBecomeLocalityDomainRegions`: two dependent calls annotated `locality_domain:0` and `locality_domain:1` become async regions on their domains in the optimized module.
- `AnnotatedCallsProduceCorrectResults`: the same program matches the interpreter's results.

head_commit.message:
PR #46000: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Backend selection and fusion wiring (PR 6/8)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the 6th in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995
PR 2/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45996
PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997
PR 4/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45998
PR 5/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999
PR 6/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000   <---- This PR
PR 7/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001
PR 8/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46002

This PR adds the xla_gpu_experimental_triton_ragged_dot flag (defaults to false) and wire up the Triton/XTile path in GemmRewriterVisitor::HandleRaggedDot().

When the flag is enabled:
- IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() validates the ragged-dot for Triton.
- A Triton/XTile fusion is created with default tile sizes.
- The existing cuDNN (CUDA) and hipBLASLt (ROCm) paths are unchanged
  and remain the default.

Also adds backend_configs.proto field for ragged-dot tile config.

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

2f4fb58c408800e5f60ba09f72af33810ba7e0eb by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Unify ragged-dot backend selection and wire up the XTile fusion

Add the xla_gpu_experimental_triton_ragged_dot flag (false by default) and
route every ragged-dot through a single function, SelectRaggedDotBackend(),
in xla/service/gpu/ir_emission_utils -- the shared utility both passes
already depend on.  It applies the priority order once:

  1a. cuDNN        - IsCudnnSupportedRaggedDot()
  1b. hipBLASLt    - IsGpublasLtSupportedGroupedMatMul()
  2.  Triton XTile - IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot()
  3.  default      - expand into a regular dot

CanBeHandledByCuDNNFusion() and CanBeHandledByGpublasltGroupGemm() moved to
ir_emission_utils as the two Is*Supported* helpers above; HandleRaggedDot()
is split into RewriteRaggedDotAsGroupedGemmCustomCall() and
RewriteRaggedDotAsTritonFusion().  When the flag is on and no higher-priority
backend claims the instruction, a kTritonFusionKind fusion is emitted with
default tile sizes.  The cuDNN and hipBLASLt paths are unchanged.

IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() restricts the XTile path to what the emitter
handles: Ampere+ on NVIDIA, one contracting and one non-contracting dimension
per side, a leading flat batch prefix, a group_sizes shape matching the
ragged mode, matching operand types apart from the mixed-FP8 pairs, and a
signed-integer group_sizes operand.

--
3ddb4fca2d5dc97f0fb0b955f0d9461757afbe93 by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Let a refused cuDNN probe fall through to another backend

SelectRaggedDotBackend() returned a single choice, so a ragged-dot that
passed the static cuDNN gates but that cuDNN had no execution plan for was
expanded into a dense dot even when the Triton XTile or gpuBLASLt path could
have taken it.

It becomes SelectRaggedDotBackends(), returning the eligible backends in
priority order; an empty result is what RaggedDotRewriter expands, so the
kDefault enumerator is gone.  Callers drop a leading kCuDnn when the cuDNN
probe refuses the ragged-dot and fall through to the next candidate.

RaggedDotRewriter and GemmRewriter must agree on the head of the list, so
GemmRewriter takes the same is_supported_by_cudnn_fusion callback, passed
from AddGemmRewriterPasses.  It only probes when the list holds a candidate
behind kCuDnn: with kCuDnn alone there is nothing to rewrite either way, and
RaggedDotRewriter has already expanded the ragged-dot if cuDNN refused it.
The autotuner pipelines are unchanged; they pass the default cudnn_version,
which keeps kCuDnn out of the list.

display_title: Stop calling Executable::set_hlo_proto in the GPU and CPU compilers

head_commit.message:
Stop calling Executable::set_hlo_proto in the GPU and CPU compilers

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The GPU and CPU compilers only attached an `HloProto` so that the
base class could answer `buffer_assignment_proto()` and so that HLO snapshots
had something to read. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` now override
`buffer_assignment_proto()` themselves, and snapshots no longer read
`Executable::hlo_proto()`, so the compilers stop calling `set_hlo_proto`.

`Executable::hlo_proto()` now returns nullptr for GPU and CPU executables. No
caller in XLA reads it anymore. `buffer_assignment_proto()` returns the same as
before.

display_title: PR #52733: [PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

head_commit.message:
PR #52733: [PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52733

Fixes jax-ml/jax#42433.

The GPU client uses stream-based usage-event compaction. In that mode `AddUsageEvent` appends any event whose definition stream isn’t known yet, and never trims the list. A copy’s source usage event is a linked promise that is only fulfilled later in `IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies`, so it always takes that path: every copy from a long-lived buffer adds one entry, and the CUDA event behind it, until the buffer is deleted.

This lets those events fall through to the trimming the non-stream branch already does: when the list is full, events that have completed (Ready or errored) are dropped before appending. A completed event has nothing left to wait for. Execute’s donation path already skips Ready events, and stream-based compaction already skips errored events when they’re added. Pending events are kept.

With the issue’s reproducer (100k `device_put` copies to `pinned_host`, RTX 4060 Ti), host memory in use went from 65.7 to 171.0 MiB before, and from 65.7 to 65.8 MiB after. New CPU, Host-platform and GPU tests fail without the change and pass with it.

Copybara import of the project:

--
f71825ada9572b7d1881fd219089b85501ea2bab by JonSnow1807 <JonSnow1807@users.noreply.github.com>:

[PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

With use_stream_based_compaction, which the GPU client sets,
AbstractTrackedDeviceBuffer::AddUsageEvent merges a new usage event into
the existing entry for its definition stream. An event whose definition
stream is not known yet is appended, and nothing in that branch ever
removes entries. Only the other branch trims events that have completed.

The source usage event of a copy is such an event. CommonCopyToMemorySpace
creates it with CreateLinkedEventPromise, and the promise is only set later
in IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies. So every CopyToMemorySpace from a
long-lived buffer, e.g. jax.device_put to another device or to pinned_host,
adds one entry, and the entries keep their CUDA events alive until the
buffer is deleted or donated. jax-ml/jax#42433 measured about 1.1 KB of
host memory per copy and source shard, without a plateau.

When the vector is full, drop the entries that are Ready before appending,
like the other branch does. A Ready usage event has completed without an
error, so Delete and the donation paths have nothing left to wait for, and
Execute already skips Ready usage events when it donates a buffer. Pending
and errored entries are kept, so per-stream merging and error propagation
do not change.

--
b99ed14ae36a18becabd36c71ae4877bc61edcdb by JonSnow1807 <JonSnow1807@users.noreply.github.com>:

[PJRT] Share usage event trimming between the compaction modes

Events that stream-based compaction can't merge now fall through to the
trimming the other mode already does, instead of a copy of it. The trim
checks the event state through the device event interface rather than
async_value(), which is null for events that aren't local AsyncValues.

Merging this change closes #52733

head_commit.message:
Remove obsolete acquire memory fence from `PopAnnotation()`.

`PopAnnotation()` executed an unconditional `std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire)` on every scope exit even when both `AnnotationStack` and NVTX were disabled. That fence worked around a 2019 header-only `thread_local` DSO split that was resolved when `AnnotationStack` moved out-of-line, and emitted an unnecessary `dmb ishld` barrier on `aarch64` CPUs on every thunk or command destructor.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Assign async Triton collective fusions to comm streams.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Assign async Triton collective fusions to comm streams.

***Problem:*** Asynchronous `__triton_collective` custom fusions wrapped in `fusion-start` are classified as compute scopes in `ExecutionStreamAssignment` and lack collective domain lookup, spreading device-barrier collectives across multiple compute streams instead of communication streams.

***Solution:*** Recognize `__triton_collective` fusions as wrapped collectives in `ExecutionStreamAssignment` and unwrap them to their inner collective hero in `collective_domain` so they are routed to the matching communication stream pool.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Schedule async Triton collective fusions as collectives.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Schedule async Triton collective fusions as collectives.

***Problem:*** The GPU latency-hiding scheduler does not recognize `fusion-start` and `fusion-done` wrapping `__triton_collective` custom fusions as async collectives, leaving them unscheduled or bypassing collective resource and device-overlap limits.

***Solution:*** Recognize async Triton collective fusions in `IsGpuAsyncStart`/`Done`, exclude them from async compute classification, unwrap them to their inner collective hero in `GpuGetCanonicalAsyncOp` and `GetParticipatingDevicesGroupsForAsyncStart`, and schedule them under collective stream resources.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Extract shared Triton collective fusion helpers.

***Problem:*** Triton collective fusion predicates are duplicated as file-local helpers in the SoL latency estimator and assume the collective instruction is always the fusion root, which breaks variadic tuple-root fusions and prevents reuse across scheduling and collective passes.

***Solution:*** Expose shared Triton collective fusion detection, hero unwrapping across sync and async wrappers, and GPU-aware async collective start/done helpers in `ir_emission_utils`, and reuse them in `SolLatencyEstimator`.

display_title: Build the OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED output of get_compiler_ir directly

head_commit.message:
Build the OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED output of get_compiler_ir directly

`GetCompilerIr` with `OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED` returned
`xla::Executable::hlo_proto()`, which XLA is removing: `Executable` becomes an
abstract base class without data members, so that loading an AOT-compiled
executable doesn't need to build the HloModule. Build the same `HloProto` from
the executable's optimized HloModule and `buffer_assignment_proto()` instead.
On CPU, literal payloads are still stripped, as the CPU compiler did when it
embedded the proto.

The output doesn't change, except that backends which never embedded an
HloProto no longer crash here. (With `--xla_dump_to` set, this used to return
the HloModule before optimizations; XLA already fixed that when it stopped
replacing the executable's HloProto for HLO snapshots.)

name: CI
display_title: [ROCm][Triton] Honor k_pack for fp4 in DecomposeAMDScaledBlocked

head_commit.message:
[ROCm][Triton] Honor k_pack for fp4 in DecomposeAMDScaledBlocked

On AMD GPUs without native scaled MFMA/WMMA (RDNA3/RDNA4, gfx90a) Triton
decomposes tt.dot_scaled via DecomposeAMDScaledBlocked. Its scaleArg unpacks
fp4 along K unconditionally and ignores lhs_k_pack/rhs_k_pack. XLA emits mxfp4
scaled dots with the RHS packed along N (rhs_k_pack = false), so the operand
was unpacked along the wrong axis and testScaledDotGeneral6-11 returned wrong
values.

Route fp4 operands that are not packed along K to the generic
DecomposeScaledBlocked::scaleArg, which unpacks along the packed dimension.

head_commit.message:
Remove obsolete acquire memory fence from `PopAnnotation()`.

`PopAnnotation()` executed an unconditional `std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire)` on every scope exit even when both `AnnotationStack` and NVTX were disabled. That fence worked around a 2019 header-only `thread_local` DSO split that was resolved when `AnnotationStack` moved out-of-line, and emitted an unnecessary `dmb ishld` barrier on `aarch64` CPUs on every thunk or command destructor.

name: CI
display_title: Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

head_commit.message:
Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The HLO that goes into HLO snapshots is debug state of whoever runs
the executable, so it moves out of `Executable::hlo_proto_`:

- `Service::BuildExecutable` returns the HLO before optimizations (plus the
  buffer assignment after optimizations) through an optional out-param instead
  of `set_hlo_proto`. `Service::Compile` keeps it in the `CompilationCache`
  entry, and `Service::Execute` reads it from there.
- `LocalExecutable` gets an optional snapshot HLO, filled through a new
  optional out-param of `LocalService::CompileExecutables`. Executables loaded
  with `LocalClient::Load` don't have one.
- New free helpers in `xla/service/executable.h`: `DumpingHloSnapshots()`
  replaces `Executable::dumping_snapshot()` at these call sites, and
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()` builds the snapshot HLO from the executable's
  HloModule and buffer assignment if nobody kept one.
- The HLO before optimizations is only built if `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots` is
  set, since snapshots are its only reader.
- The CPU AOT loader no longer attaches a full HloProto when dumping snapshots;
  the fallback above produces the same content.
- Deletes the unused `HloRunnerLegacy::HloProtoFromWrapped`.

Behaviour change: snapshot paths that dereferenced a null `hlo_proto()` before
(e.g. CPU without `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, GPU executables loaded from a
proto, `Service::ExecuteGraphParallel` on CPU) now dump the optimized HloModule
instead of crashing. On CPU with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, these snapshots
now keep literal payloads. Snapshots that contain the HLO before optimizations
today still do. Since `Service` no longer replaces the executable's HloProto,
TF's `get_compiler_ir` with `OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED` now returns the
optimized module also when dumping is enabled. It returned the module before
optimizations in that case, which was a bug.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025395036

name: CI
display_title: Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

head_commit.message:
Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. `hlo_proto_` on the base mixes up two things: the buffer assignment
that the backend owns, and an HLO snapshot that the creator attaches for
dumping. This CL starts to pull them apart.

`Executable::buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes virtual. The default still
reads `hlo_proto_`. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` override it from state
they own, and return it in exactly the cases where the base accessor returns
non-null today:

- `GpuExecutable` returns its buffer assignment proto only if the compiler
  embeds debug info and keeps the HloModule
  (`Params::expose_buffer_assignment_proto`). Executables loaded from a proto
  still return nullptr. The always-available GPU accessor is renamed to
  `owned_buffer_assignment_proto()`, because a non-virtual accessor with the
  same name would hide the virtual one.
- `CpuExecutable` gets an optional buffer assignment proto that the CPU
  compiler sets with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, and the CPU AOT loader with
  `xla_embed_ir_in_executable` or `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots`.

The compilers still call `set_hlo_proto`; that goes away in a follow-up.

No behaviour change.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025395053

name: CI
display_title: Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

head_commit.message:
Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule. With the HloModule stored in the base class, every executable
had to carry one to answer metadata queries.

Move `hlo_module_` and `module_stats_` and the implementations that read them
into `HloModuleExecutable`:

- `shared_module()` (nullable), `module_config()`, `result_shape()`,
  `compute_computation_layout()`, `name()`, `input_output_alias_config()`,
  `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()` are pure virtual on
  `Executable`. `set_module_stats()` lives on `HloModuleExecutable`.
- `module()` and `has_module()` stay as non-virtual helpers on top of a new
  protected pure virtual `module_ptr()`, so they don't copy a
  `std::shared_ptr`.
- Virtuals that don't need state keep their defaults
  (`SizeOfGeneratedCodeInBytes()`, `GetAllocations()`, ...).
- The unused `execution_count_` is deleted.

The only state left in `Executable` is the HLO proto for debugging
(`hlo_proto_` and its mutex). It still fills in the module lazily through
`module()`. Later changes move its producers and readers away and remove it.

`HloModuleExecutable` implements everything from the module as before, so
there is no behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that
derive from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable`
instead (or implement the new pure virtuals).

display_title: PR #46000: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Backend selection and fusion wiring (PR 6/8)

head_commit.message:
PR #46000: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Backend selection and fusion wiring (PR 6/8)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the 6th in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995
PR 2/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45996
PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997
PR 4/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45998
PR 5/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999
PR 6/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000   <---- This PR
PR 7/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001
PR 8/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46002

This PR adds the xla_gpu_experimental_triton_ragged_dot flag (defaults to false) and wire up the Triton/XTile path in GemmRewriterVisitor::HandleRaggedDot().

When the flag is enabled:
- IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() validates the ragged-dot for Triton.
- A Triton/XTile fusion is created with default tile sizes.
- The existing cuDNN (CUDA) and hipBLASLt (ROCm) paths are unchanged
  and remain the default.

Also adds backend_configs.proto field for ragged-dot tile config.

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply:⚡️ Performance Improvement, ✨ New Feature

A few performance numbers:

| 32,768 | 6,144 | 16,384 | 8 | 20,966 | 314.65 | 65,785 | 100.28 |
| 32,768 | 16,384 | 6,144 | 8 | 22,489 | 293.35 | 65,128 | 101.29 |
| 49,152 | 1,408 | 2,048 | 64 | 1,307 | 216.95 | 35,787 | 7.92 |
| 393,216 | 2,048 | 1,408 | 64 | 7,315 | 310.03 | – | – |
| 3,145,728 | 2,048 | 1,408 | 8 | 53,108 | 341.60 | – | – |

#### Ragged dimension in contracting dimension, dtype = f16

| M | K | N | G | Triton (µs) | Triton (TFLOPS) | Baseline (µs) | Baseline (TFLOPS) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

2f4fb58c408800e5f60ba09f72af33810ba7e0eb by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Unify ragged-dot backend selection and wire up the XTile fusion

Add the xla_gpu_experimental_triton_ragged_dot flag (false by default) and
route every ragged-dot through a single function, SelectRaggedDotBackend(),
in xla/service/gpu/ir_emission_utils -- the shared utility both passes
already depend on.  It applies the priority order once:

  1a. cuDNN        - IsCudnnSupportedRaggedDot()
  1b. hipBLASLt    - IsGpublasLtSupportedGroupedMatMul()
  2.  Triton XTile - IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot()
  3.  default      - expand into a regular dot

CanBeHandledByCuDNNFusion() and CanBeHandledByGpublasltGroupGemm() moved to
ir_emission_utils as the two Is*Supported* helpers above; HandleRaggedDot()
is split into RewriteRaggedDotAsGroupedGemmCustomCall() and
RewriteRaggedDotAsTritonFusion().  When the flag is on and no higher-priority
backend claims the instruction, a kTritonFusionKind fusion is emitted with
default tile sizes.  The cuDNN and hipBLASLt paths are unchanged.

IsTritonSupportedRaggedDot() restricts the XTile path to what the emitter
handles: Ampere+ on NVIDIA, one contracting and one non-contracting dimension
per side, a leading flat batch prefix, a group_sizes shape matching the
ragged mode, matching operand types apart from the mixed-FP8 pairs, and a
signed-integer group_sizes operand.

3ddb4fca2d5dc97f0fb0b955f0d9461757afbe93 by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Let a refused cuDNN probe fall through to another backend

SelectRaggedDotBackend() returned a single choice, so a ragged-dot that
passed the static cuDNN gates but that cuDNN had no execution plan for was
expanded into a dense dot even when the Triton XTile or gpuBLASLt path could
have taken it.

It becomes SelectRaggedDotBackends(), returning the eligible backends in
priority order; an empty result is what RaggedDotRewriter expands, so the
kDefault enumerator is gone.  Callers drop a leading kCuDnn when the cuDNN
probe refuses the ragged-dot and fall through to the next candidate.

RaggedDotRewriter and GemmRewriter must agree on the head of the list, so
GemmRewriter takes the same is_supported_by_cudnn_fusion callback, passed
from AddGemmRewriterPasses.  It only probes when the list holds a candidate
behind kCuDnn: with kCuDnn alone there is nothing to rewrite either way, and
RaggedDotRewriter has already expanded the ragged-dot if cuDNN refused it.
The autotuner pipelines are unchanged; they pass the default cudnn_version,
which keeps kCuDnn out of the list.

display_title: Remove obsolete acquire memory fence from `PopAnnotation()`.

head_commit.message:
Remove obsolete acquire memory fence from `PopAnnotation()`.

`PopAnnotation()` executed an unconditional `std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire)` on every scope exit even when both `AnnotationStack` and NVTX were disabled. That fence worked around a 2019 header-only `thread_local` DSO split that was resolved when `AnnotationStack` moved out-of-line, and emitted an unnecessary `dmb ishld` barrier on `aarch64` CPUs on every thunk or command destructor.

name: CI
display_title: Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

head_commit.message:
Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

The goal is to avoid loading the `HloModule` when an executable is loaded in
an AOT setup. Deserializing the module is expensive, and a loaded executable
only needs it for debugging (dumps, profiling, introspection). But today
`Executable` owns the `HloModule` and answers metadata queries (module config,
entry computation layout, input/output aliasing, ...) from it, so every
backend and every caller depends on the module being there.

So `Executable` is going to become an abstract base class without data
members. Executables that keep the HloModule they were compiled from derive
from a new `HloModuleExecutable`, which implements today's behaviour.
Executables that don't need the module at runtime (like `GpuExecutable` for
loaded AOT executables) can then implement the interface without it.

As a first step this adds `HloModuleExecutable` in
`xla/service/hlo_module_executable.h`. For now it only forwards the
constructor to `Executable`; the module related members move there in a
follow-up.

`GpuExecutable`, `CpuExecutable`, `InterpreterExecutableBase` and the test
fakes in `xla/service/executable_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/gpu_profiler_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/autotuner/autotuner_test.cc` and
`xla/backends/autotuner/config_runner_test.cc` now derive from
`HloModuleExecutable` instead of `Executable`.

No behaviour change.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Ignore process_index in CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Ignore process_index in CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint

`GetPjRtCpuClient` populates each process's local `CpuTopology` with that worker's `process_id`, and `CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()` hashes the serialized `CpuTopologyProto` directly. In homogeneous multi-process CPU jobs, every worker therefore computes a different topology fingerprint even though `process_index` has no effect on XLA:CPU compilation. Downstream caches like JAX's persistent compilation cache hash the topology fingerprint, so non-zero processes miss cache entries written by process 0 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So this change clears `process_index` on the `CpuTopologyProto` copy in `CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()`, while still hashing device count, local hardware IDs, and target machine options.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Use HloModule::GetFingerprint128 for PjRtCpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Use HloModule::GetFingerprint128 for PjRtCpuExecutable

`PjRtCpuExecutable` currently hashes `HloModule::ToString()` for its executable fingerprint and returns early before computing a fingerprint when a module has zero parameters. Default HLO printing includes `OpMetadata`, where `HloModule::CanonicalizeStackFrameIds` renumbers stack frame IDs in computation order during proto deserialization. When optimization passes introduce callee subcomputations that serialize before `ENTRY`, a deserialized executable gets a different fingerprint than the freshly compiled one. In multi-process CPU runs with Gloo collectives, asymmetric persistent cache hits then derive different `RunId`s and Gloo tags across processes, causing collectives to hang (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So let's compute `fingerprint_` with `HloModule::GetFingerprint128()` before the zero-parameter early return, matching `PjRtStreamExecutorClient`. This omits metadata from the fingerprint, avoids materializing the full HLO text in memory, and gives zero-parameter modules a valid fingerprint.

72c0c434e968b61d917b8a800096a926a15004d1 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations by default

Flip the default of
`xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` to true.

The flag only takes effect with COLLECTIVES in
`xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED command

an output allocation is re-recorded on every execution, because the output
allocation gets a new address each time. Keeping these buffers in the temp
allocation gives them a stable address, so the recorded collective is
skipped at initialization.

buffers) is unchanged. Setting the flag to false restores the previous
behavior.

[XLA][NFC] Move service/fusion_explorer to tools/fusion_explorer

Move Fusion Explorer web viewer assets (`simple_viewer.html`, `viewer.html`, and
`viewer_server.py`) and their header-embedding `genrule` targets out of
`xla/service` into a dedicated `xla/tools/fusion_explorer` package, exposing
them via `//xla/tools/fusion_explorer:fusion_explorer_embed` for
`hlo_graph_dumper`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Disable external NCCL net plugins by default in multi-process GPU tests.

Single-host multi-process GPU tests do not need external network plugins, which can spawn background threads that race with leak checking on worker exit.

head_commit.message:
Link `test_main` in `traceme_encode_test` and `scoped_annotation_test`.

Both test targets register `BENCHMARK(...)` microbenchmarks via `//xla/tsl/platform:test_benchmark` while linking `@com_google_googletest//:gtest_main`, which ignores `--benchmark_filter` and runs zero benchmarks. Link `//xla/tsl/platform:test_main` instead so both unit tests and microbenchmarks can execute.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Use HloModule::GetFingerprint128 for PjRtCpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Use HloModule::GetFingerprint128 for PjRtCpuExecutable

`PjRtCpuExecutable` currently hashes `HloModule::ToString()` for its executable fingerprint and returns early before computing a fingerprint when a module has zero parameters. Default HLO printing includes `OpMetadata`, where `HloModule::CanonicalizeStackFrameIds` renumbers stack frame IDs in computation order during proto deserialization. When optimization passes introduce callee subcomputations that serialize before `ENTRY`, a deserialized executable gets a different fingerprint than the freshly compiled one. In multi-process CPU runs with Gloo collectives, asymmetric persistent cache hits then derive different `RunId`s and Gloo tags across processes, causing collectives to hang (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So let's compute `fingerprint_` with `HloModule::GetFingerprint128()` before the zero-parameter early return, matching `PjRtStreamExecutorClient`. This omits metadata from the fingerprint, avoids materializing the full HLO text in memory, and gives zero-parameter modules a valid fingerprint.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Ignore process_index in CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Ignore process_index in CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint

`GetPjRtCpuClient` populates each process's local `CpuTopology` with that worker's `process_id`, and `CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()` hashes the serialized `CpuTopologyProto` directly. In homogeneous multi-process CPU jobs, every worker therefore computes a different topology fingerprint even though `process_index` has no effect on XLA:CPU compilation. Downstream caches like JAX's persistent compilation cache hash the topology fingerprint, so non-zero processes miss cache entries written by process 0 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So this change clears `process_index` on the `CpuTopologyProto` copy in `CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()`, while still hashing device count, local hardware IDs, and target machine options.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Reject `Unknown` and `ShardGroup` `xla::HloSharding`s in `HloSharding` and `HloShardingSpec`

`xla::ifrt::HloSharding` and `xla::ifrt::HloShardingSpec` model concrete leaf array shardings, yet still accepted compiler-internal `Unknown` and `ShardGroup` `xla::HloSharding` instances during construction and `SerDes` deserialization (`Unknown` still `CHECK`-failed in `xla::HloSharding::ToNamedSharding()`, while `ShardGroup` is a compiler-only propagation annotation whose `shard_group_id == -1` form is silently dropped by `ToProto()`), and `HloShardingSpec::IndexDomains` skipped shape-rank validation on non-replicated subgroup shardings before calling `TileOffsetForDevice()`. In addition, `HloShardingSpecSerDes` lacked the `HloShardingV3` (`named_sharding`) serialization and deserialization guards present in `HloShardingSerDes`, and `HloShardingSerDes` inherited from `RTTIExtends<HloSharding, SerDes>` instead of `RTTIExtends<HloShardingSerDes, SerDes>`.

Reject `IsUnknown()` and any non-default `ShardGroup` (`!(GetShardGroup() == NotShardGroup())`) in `HloShardingSpec::CreateIfValid`, remove the now-unreachable `IsUnknown()` branches in `HloShardingSpec`, validate `shape.dims().size() == TiledDataRank()` before `HasNonReplicatedSubgroup()` in `HloShardingSpec::IndexDomains`, reject `HloShardingV3` (`named_sharding`) in `HloShardingSpecSerDes` via a shared `ContainsNamedSharding` helper, and fix `HloShardingSerDes`'s RTTI base class.

display_title: PR #53387: [XLA:GPU] Resolve async-start through async intermediaries in LHS GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit

head_commit.message:
PR #53387: [XLA:GPU] Resolve async-start through async intermediaries in LHS GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53387

📝 Summary of Changes

`GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit` was assuming that the async-start corresponding to a candidate async-done is always the done's first operand. This is not the case when the start reaches the done through intermediary instructions (e.g. `tuple`, `opt-barrier`, `get-tuple-element`, etc). This PR uses the `FindStart()` helper to resolve the async-start through intermediaries. If `FindStart` cannot resolve a start in the computation being scheduled, the function conservatively reports that the overlap limit is crossed.

Limitations:
- Overlapping a collective with a loop-carried future is unsupported. This is because `FindStart()` only returns an async-start if the start is in the same computation as the done, which isn't the case with while ops (the done in the body has a start reachable from the caller computation).
- Implementing collective overlap with loop-carried futures is complicated by the fact that many of the async utils assume that each done has a unique start, which is not the case with loop-carried futures (we have one start before the loop body, and one inside the body from the previous iteration). Support for loop-carried futures will be improved in follow-up PRs; this PR fixes cases where an async start and done are in the same computation.
- Several LHS functions other than `GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit` (e.g. `CanonicalAsyncStart`, `IsAnnotatedForGpuAsyncStreamCollectivesP2P`, `IsCollectivesGroupAsyncDoneOp`) also assume that the done's first operand is the start. Follow-up PRs will address those functions.

🎯 Justification

Without this fix, when collective multi-streaming is enabled or the module uses multiple collective communication domains, an async collective whose async-done does not consume its async-start directly is never allowed to overlap another in-flight collective. This needlessly serializes collectives, and when data dependencies force the overlap, the LHS fails to schedule valid HLO. `OverlapLimitResolvesAsyncStartThroughIntermediaries` demonstrates the failing case.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `gpu_latency_hiding_scheduler_test.cc`:

- `OverlapLimitResolvesAsyncStartThroughIntermediaries`: schedules HLO with two async all-gathers whose starts and dones are separated by an `opt-barrier`. Both must be in flight at the same time and each `async-done` reaches its `async-start` through `tuple`, `opt-barrier`, and `get-tuple-element`. The two all-gathers share at most one device, so this is allowed. Without this PR's change, scheduling fails with `FindAndExtractBestNodeAvailable failed to find a node to schedule`.
- `OverlapLimitRejectsLoopCarriedAsyncDoneWithUnknownStart`: schedules HLO with a pipelined all-gather whose start is carried into the while body from the previous iteration. `opt-barrier`s force another all-gather to be in flight when the carried `async-done` is scheduled, and since the start is not in the same computation as the done, the scheduler conservatively refuses to overlap them even though they share at most one device.

display_title: Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

head_commit.message:
Add `start_capture`, `stop_capture`, and `capture` to `jax.profiler`.

Nsight Systems (`nsys --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi`) and Nsight Compute (`ncu --profile-from-start off`) only record what runs between `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop`. JAX users currently call these through custom `ctypes` wrappers.

`jax.profiler.start_capture()`, `jax.profiler.stop_capture()`, and the `jax.profiler.capture()` context manager call new `_profiler.start_capture` and `_profiler.stop_capture` bindings. The bindings load `cuProfilerStart` and `cuProfilerStop` from `libcuda.so.1` at first use and raise an error if the driver is missing or the call fails. The calling thread needs a current CUDA context, which it has once it ran a JAX computation. The JAX functions raise `RuntimeError` on non-CUDA backends and on older jaxlib builds without the bindings.

display_title: [XLA] Reenable support for ALG_DOT_BF16_BF16_F32_X9 in ConvertDotAlgorithm

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reenable support for ALG_DOT_BF16_BF16_F32_X9 in ConvertDotAlgorithm

Silently dropping `ALG_DOT_BF16_BF16_F32_X9` causes Triton GEMM fusions to compute TF32 accuracy (~2.9e-4 relative error) instead of BF16x9 accuracy (~1e-7) with no compiler error, and breaks HLO-to-StableHLO import for X9 dots.

head_commit.message:
PR #53299: [XLA:GPU] Auto-enable keeping recorded collectives out of output allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53299

📝 Summary of Changes

`xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` is now enabled automatically when `COLLECTIVES` is in `xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the command buffer update mode is `SKIP_TEMP` or `SKIP_PROFILED`. In any other configuration it stays disabled. An explicit value of the flag takes priority.

This is the follow-up to https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52104, which added the flag with default off.

🎯 Justification

In these modes a collective whose buffer shares an output allocation is re-recorded on every execution. The flag avoids that at the cost of some temp memory. Users who select these modes should get this without knowing about a second flag.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

72c0c434e968b61d917b8a800096a926a15004d1 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations by default

Flip the default of
`xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` to true.

The flag only takes effect with COLLECTIVES in
`xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED command
buffer update mode. In that configuration a collective whose buffer shares
an output allocation is re-recorded on every execution, because the output
allocation gets a new address each time. Keeping these buffers in the temp
allocation gives them a stable address, so the recorded collective is
skipped at initialization.

The default configuration (ALWAYS_UPDATE, COLLECTIVES not in command
buffers) is unchanged. Setting the flag to false restores the previous
behavior.

--
fb92f6f2cd2378c767b79b09615fb97a82df8858 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Auto-enable keeping collectives out of outputs from presence

Leave `xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` unset by
default instead of defaulting it to true. When it is not set, it is
enabled with COLLECTIVES in `xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the
SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED update mode, and disabled otherwise. An
explicit value takes priority.

--
133df5762d94d5a4cfffbde646ac081d9a4f7aa5 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Make an explicit keep-collectives-out-of-outputs value always win

When xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs is unset it is
enabled automatically if COLLECTIVES is in xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer and
the update mode is SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED, and disabled otherwise. An
explicit true or false now takes priority in every configuration.

The resolution lives in one helper returning a Decision. GetNonDefaultDebugOptions
now also compares presence for fields with explicit presence, so an explicit
false is kept in *.debug_options dumps instead of being dropped as equal to the
unset default. The flag help and proto comment describe the three states.

--

[XLA:GPU] Address review comments on keep-collectives-out-of-outputs tests and dump

Merging this change closes #53299

In Triton GEMM fusions, the missing attribute lowers to a single TF32 `tt.dot` instead of the requested algorithm, causing silent accuracy loss.

display_title: Remove obsolete acquire memory fence from `PopAnnotation()`.

head_commit.message:
Remove obsolete acquire memory fence from `PopAnnotation()`.

`PopAnnotation()` executed an unconditional `std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire)` on every scope exit even when both `AnnotationStack` and NVTX were disabled. That fence worked around a 2019 header-only `thread_local` DSO split that was resolved when `AnnotationStack` moved out-of-line, and emitted an unnecessary `dmb ishld` barrier on `aarch64` CPUs on every thunk or command destructor.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023578328

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Replace reduction tile pruning with strided opt-in selection

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Replace reduction tile pruning with strided opt-in selection

Pruning was wasteful as a strategy as it still hits the compile-time due to trying many configurations that aren't useful. Instead, the microbenchmarks were analyzed to see where we improve with tiling reduction dimensions. This change uses an opt-in strategy instead.

The most impactful cases were shown to be column reductions. For these cases tiling the reduce dimension allows us to use bigger tiles for minor parallel dimensions that can benefit from coalescing. The thresholds used are empirical from the data, but they look reasonable.

The change only applies behind flags, so production is unaffected. Follow-up changes will modify the cost model to improve the top-1 candidates and enable tiled reductions for kernels with no more than one reduce op.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025374839

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add a symmetric memory cache API to GPU communicators.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add a symmetric memory cache API to GPU communicators.

Adds `GpuCommunicator::AcquireSymmetricMemory` and `ReleaseSymmetricMemory`. `AcquireSymmetricMemory` returns a shared registration that stays cached on the communicator until `ReleaseSymmetricMemory` is called for the same address or the communicator is destroyed or aborted. The default implementation falls back to an uncached `CreateSymmetricMemory`.

This cache is not used yet it will be needed later to move NCCL window registration from executable level to the NCCL communicator level.

name: CI
display_title: Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

head_commit.message:
Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Reusing these buffers as well lowers the peak memory, but a reused buffer stays at the same offset for longer, which can increase the fragmentation by more than the reuse saves. So always reusing them makes some modules smaller and others larger.

Therefore this change adds `HeapSimulator::RunWithBeneficialOperandReuse`, which `BufferAssigner` now uses. If a heap simulation reused such a buffer, the allocs and frees are replayed without this kind of reuse (new `HeapSimulator::Options::may_reuse_operand_buffers_through_other_positions`), and the reuse is only kept if it results in a smaller heap.

Comparing the heaps needs a second `HeapAlgorithm::Finish()`, which is slow on large modules for the `kSpatial` and `kTemporal` packing strategies. So for algorithms without a fast `Finish()` (new `HeapAlgorithm::HasFastFinish()`), the reuse is dropped right away if it does not lower the peak memory. Stats-only runs (`NoFragmentationStatsHeap` in `MinimumMemoryForModule`) stay restricted to direct operands so schedule scoring in `DefaultMemoryScheduler` does not change.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Replace reduction tile pruning with strided opt-in selection

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Replace reduction tile pruning with strided opt-in selection

Pruning was wasteful as a strategy as it still hits the compile-time due to trying many configurations that aren't useful. Instead, the microbenchmarks were analyzed to see where we improve with tiling reduction dimensions. This change uses an opt-in strategy instead.

The most impactful cases were shown to be column reductions. For these cases tiling the reduce dimension allows us to use bigger tiles for minor parallel dimensions that can benefit from coalescing. The thresholds used are empirical from the data, but they look reasonable.

The change only applies behind flags, so production is unaffected. Follow-up changes will modify the cost model to improve the top-1 candidates and enable tiled reductions for kernels with no more than one reduce op.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

Previously, the MLIR bitonic sort emitter only fused compare-and-swap steps
within one CTA's shared-memory tile (`tile_size`), requiring a separate global
kernel launch per step once `xor_mask >= tile_size`.

On Hopper+ GPUs (`sm_90+`), extend tiled bitonic sort across 2-CTA clusters
using distributed shared memory (DSMEM) and cluster barriers, doubling the
in-kernel sort span and cutting global round-trips:
- Add `gpu::BarrierScope` (default `Workgroup`) to `xla_gpu.sync_threads`
  and forward it to `gpu.barrier` in `LowerTensors` so `GPUToNVVM` lowers
  cluster barriers to `nvvm.cluster.arrive` and `nvvm.cluster.wait`.
- Add `xla_gpu.dsmem_pointer`, emit it for `"xla_gpu.dsmem"` shared-memory
  accesses in `LowerTensors`, and lower it to `nvvm.mapa` in
  `LowerToLLVMGPUPass` so `LowerTensorsPass` adds no GPU dialect dependencies.
- Emit 2-CTA clustered bitonic sort kernels when stages exceed `tile_size`,
  unclustered blocks exceed SM count, and cluster padding is at most 12.5%
  (capping at 2 CTAs avoids GPC fragmentation and register pressure). Cross-CTA
  steps use `gpu.cluster_block_id x` and DSMEM; full tiles keep the unrolled
  fast path while bounds-checked and post-cluster `kIntraTileSort` merges stay
  rolled.
- Verify end-to-end cluster dimension propagation through
  `CubinCustomKernelCompiler`.

head_commit.message:
PR #52810: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52810

📝 Summary of Changes

Add RocmVmmAllocator::Options with an enable_posix_fd_handle flag and thread it through every ROCm VMM site, centralizing the property setup and granularity query in GetRocmVmmAllocationParams(). The four sites previously built properties by hand, risking a granularity queried with properties that differ from the ones used to allocate; a reservation and the allocations mapped into it must agree on it.

The flag defaults to true, as CudaDeviceAllocator::Options does, so every ROCm VMM site requests exportable handles unless a caller opts out.

Exportable handles are requested only on ROCm 10.0+ (HIP 7.15+); earlier runtimes cannot export and import them correctly, so the request is dropped with a warning rather than failing the allocation. The runtime version is necessary but not sufficient — the kernel driver, the container or the device may still refuse fd export — so a rejected granularity query or hipMemCreate() falls back to hipMemHandleTypeNone with a warning, as the CUDA allocator does. Workloads that never export keep running.

🎯 Justification

Collective libraries share buffers by exporting their allocation handles as POSIX file descriptors, but ROCm VMM allocations were created with hipMemHandleTypeNone, which permits no export at all.

🚀 Kind of Contribution: ✨ New Feature

🧪 Unit Tests: Add rocm_vmm_exportable_handles_test, covering the option in both directions, the fallback leaving allocation intact, an export/import round trip, and a collective-space buffer from the kVmm allocator.

head_commit.message:
PR #53299: [XLA:GPU] Auto-enable keeping recorded collectives out of output allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53299

📝 Summary of Changes

`xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` is now enabled automatically when `COLLECTIVES` is in `xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the command buffer update mode is `SKIP_TEMP` or `SKIP_PROFILED`. In any other configuration it stays disabled. An explicit value of the flag takes priority.

This is the follow-up to https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52104, which added the flag with default off.

🎯 Justification

In these modes a collective whose buffer shares an output allocation is re-recorded on every execution. The flag avoids that at the cost of some temp memory. Users who select these modes should get this without knowing about a second flag.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

72c0c434e968b61d917b8a800096a926a15004d1 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations by default

Flip the default of
`xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` to true.

The flag only takes effect with COLLECTIVES in
`xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED command
buffer update mode. In that configuration a collective whose buffer shares
an output allocation is re-recorded on every execution, because the output
allocation gets a new address each time. Keeping these buffers in the temp
allocation gives them a stable address, so the recorded collective is
skipped at initialization.

The default configuration (ALWAYS_UPDATE, COLLECTIVES not in command
buffers) is unchanged. Setting the flag to false restores the previous
behavior.

--
