[XLA:GPU] Auto-enable keeping collectives out of outputs from presence

Leave `xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` unset by
default instead of defaulting it to true. When it is not set, it is
enabled with COLLECTIVES in `xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the
SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED update mode, and disabled otherwise. An
explicit value takes priority.

--
133df5762d94d5a4cfffbde646ac081d9a4f7aa5 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Make an explicit keep-collectives-out-of-outputs value always win

When xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs is unset it is
enabled automatically if COLLECTIVES is in xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer and
the update mode is SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED, and disabled otherwise. An
explicit true or false now takes priority in every configuration.

The resolution lives in one helper returning a Decision. GetNonDefaultDebugOptions
now also compares presence for fields with explicit presence, so an explicit
false is kept in *.debug_options dumps instead of being dropped as equal to the
unset default. The flag help and proto comment describe the three states.

Merging this change closes #53299

head_commit.message:
PR #53417: [XLA:GPU][SPIR-V] Use SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic for SPIR-V bf16 arithmetic

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53417

A recent LLVM commit https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/d69921f87c7f59e867d643af6cb23edd34353f23 that was part of the last LLVM update renamed the `SPV_INTEL_bfloat16_arithmetic` extension to `SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic`. Since the spirv backend still referenced the old enum value, the oneAPI CI build broke.
This PR updates the extension set to use the new `SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic` name, so the oneAPI build compiles again.

Note: This is the first part of the fix because the underlying drivers still expect the old extension name and might reject SPIR-V modules that declare the new extension.

PR #52810: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52810

📝 Summary of Changes

Add RocmVmmAllocator::Options with an enable_posix_fd_handle flag and thread it through every ROCm VMM site, centralizing the property setup and granularity query in GetRocmVmmAllocationParams(). The four sites previously built properties by hand, risking a granularity queried with properties that differ from the ones used to allocate; a reservation and the allocations mapped into it must agree on it.

The flag defaults to true, as CudaDeviceAllocator::Options does, so every ROCm VMM site requests exportable handles unless a caller opts out.

Exportable handles are requested only on ROCm 10.0+ (HIP 7.15+); earlier runtimes cannot export and import them correctly, so the request is dropped with a warning rather than failing the allocation. The runtime version is necessary but not sufficient — the kernel driver, the container or the device may still refuse fd export — so a rejected granularity query or hipMemCreate() falls back to hipMemHandleTypeNone with a warning, as the CUDA allocator does. Workloads that never export keep running.

🎯 Justification

Collective libraries share buffers by exporting their allocation handles as POSIX file descriptors, but ROCm VMM allocations were created with hipMemHandleTypeNone, which permits no export at all.

🚀 Kind of Contribution: ✨ New Feature

🧪 Unit Tests: Add rocm_vmm_exportable_handles_test, covering the option in both directions, the fallback leaving allocation intact, an export/import round trip, and a collective-space buffer from the kVmm allocator.

previously built properties by hand, risking a granularity queried with
properties that differ from the ones used to allocate; a reservation and
the allocations mapped into it must agree on it. The ROCm

Exportable handles are requested only on ROCm 10.0+ (HIP 7.15+); earlier

display_title: Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

head_commit.message:
Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

The goal is to avoid loading the `HloModule` when an executable is loaded in
an AOT setup. Deserializing the module is expensive, and a loaded executable
only needs it for debugging (dumps, profiling, introspection). But today
`Executable` owns the `HloModule` and answers metadata queries (module config,
entry computation layout, input/output aliasing, ...) from it, so every
backend and every caller depends on the module being there.

So `Executable` is going to become an abstract base class without data
members. Executables that keep the HloModule they were compiled from derive
from a new `HloModuleExecutable`, which implements today's behaviour.
Executables that don't need the module at runtime (like `GpuExecutable` for
loaded AOT executables) can then implement the interface without it.

As a first step this adds `HloModuleExecutable` in
`xla/service/hlo_module_executable.h`. For now it only forwards the
constructor to `Executable`; the module related members move there in a
follow-up.

`GpuExecutable`, `CpuExecutable`, `InterpreterExecutableBase` and the test
fakes in `xla/service/executable_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/gpu_profiler_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/autotuner/autotuner_test.cc` and
`xla/backends/autotuner/config_runner_test.cc` now derive from
`HloModuleExecutable` instead of `Executable`.

No behaviour change.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add a symmetric memory cache API to GPU communicators.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add a symmetric memory cache API to GPU communicators.

Adds `GpuCommunicator::AcquireSymmetricMemory` and `ReleaseSymmetricMemory`. `AcquireSymmetricMemory` returns a shared registration that stays cached on the communicator until `ReleaseSymmetricMemory` is called for the same address or the communicator is destroyed or aborted. The default implementation falls back to an uncached `CreateSymmetricMemory`.

This cache is not used yet it will be needed later to move NCCL window registration from executable level to the NCCL communicator level.

display_title: PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

head_commit.message:
PR #52821: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52821

📝 Summary of Changes

Lets an XLA program run a computation on a chosen locality domain by annotating a call with `_xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>"`. Builds on the stream building blocks ([#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124)) and their execution support ([#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302)).
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper`: wraps a locality-domain-annotated call into an async region. It rejects regions that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and annotations that aren't on a non-inlineable call.
- `ExecutionStreamAssignment`: assigns `LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>)` to those regions, without using up a round-robin compute stream.
- `AsyncStartThunk::Prepare`: rejects communication thunks inside a locality-domain region at runtime.
- **MHLO → HLO**: stream annotations stay on the call, not on the get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.
- `side_effect_util`: adds `kXlaLocalityDomainStreamAnnotationPrefix` (`"locality_domain:"`).

🎯 Justification

This is the first PR that lets a program annotate calls to run on a locality domain's stream, using the runtime support from [#52246](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52302). Programs without these annotations are unchanged.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this enables locality-domain execution

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `ExecutionStreamAssignmentTest`:
  - `ValidLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.AssignsLocalityDomainStream`;
  - `MalformedLocalityDomainAnnotationTest.DiesWithCheckMessage`;
  - `LocalityDomainAnnotationRejectsCommunicationScope`;
  - `LocalityDomainDoesNotConsumeRoundRobinStream`.
- `ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapperTest` (10 tests):
  - wrapping a call while keeping its attributes; idempotence; tuple calls with get-tuple-element users;
  - rejecting missing or inlineable calls, transitive collectives, nested annotations and send/recv;
  - returning an error status inside fusions and async computations.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainPrepareRejectsCommunicationThunks`: a compute-only region prepares successfully, and one containing a communication thunk is rejected.
- `frontend_attributes.mlir`: stream annotations aren't copied onto the get-tuple-elements of a multi-result call.

🧪 Execution Tests:

`LocalityDomainComputeTest` runs on a single GPU, and skips on GPUs with fewer than two locality domains.
- `AnnotatedCallsBecomeLocalityDomainRegions`: two dependent calls annotated `locality_domain:0` and `locality_domain:1` become async regions on their domains in the optimized module.
- `AnnotatedCallsProduceCorrectResults`: the same program matches the interpreter's results.

e7e813477d5b08386aaf577217b60473aa2a60aa by Keshav <keshavb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

A call annotated with _xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>" is
wrapped into an async region by ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper and
assigned LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>) by ExecutionStreamAssignment, so it
runs on that domain's stream. The wrapper rejects locality-domain regions
that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and
AsyncStartThunk::Prepare rejects communication thunks inside them at
runtime. Stream annotations are kept only on the call, not on the
get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.

Merging this change closes #52821

display_title: PR #53417: [XLA:GPU][SPIR-V] Use SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic for SPIR-V bf16 arithmetic

head_commit.message:
PR #53417: [XLA:GPU][SPIR-V] Use SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic for SPIR-V bf16 arithmetic

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53417

A recent LLVM commit https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/d69921f87c7f59e867d643af6cb23edd34353f23 that was part of the last LLVM update renamed the `SPV_INTEL_bfloat16_arithmetic` extension to `SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic`. Since the spirv backend still referenced the old enum value, the oneAPI CI build broke.
This PR updates the extension set to use the new `SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic` name, so the oneAPI build compiles again.

Note: This is the first part of the fix because the underlying drivers still expect the old extension name and might reject SPIR-V modules that declare the new extension.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Require K>=32 for 8-bit Triton dot operands on CUDA

NVIDIA 8-bit MMA uses K=32. The Triton search space allowed 16, which produced 2x results. Enforce 32 in the search space and both verifiers, and reject smaller explicit configs. Bump the Triton and autotune cache versions.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Validate and annotate CTA cluster dimensions on LLVM kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Validate and annotate CTA cluster dimensions on LLVM kernels

`AnnotateKernelLaunchDimensions` previously ignored optional CTA cluster
dimensions on `LaunchDimensions` and did not attach the `"nvvm.cluster_dim"`
LLVM function attribute needed to lower `.reqnctapercluster` in PTX.

Reject cluster dimensions in `AnnotateKernelLaunchDimensions` on non-NVPTX or
pre-Hopper targets, when any coordinate is non-positive, or when `block_counts`
is not divisible by `cluster_dims`. Attach `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` to the kernel
function when `cluster_dims` is set.

name: CI
display_title: [IFRT IR] Adopt `CalleeSymbolManager` in `IfrtPopulateAtomProgramMetadataPass`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Adopt `CalleeSymbolManager` in `IfrtPopulateAtomProgramMetadataPass`

`IfrtPopulateAtomProgramMetadataPass` previously tracked callees with a reverse walk that cloned temporary `CallOp`s as map keys and mutated private outlined modules without isolating internal `func.call` references. When call-site variants were interleaved (e.g., variant A, variant B, variant A), the reverse walk also caused the later variant to claim the original `@callee` name while cloning the earliest variant.

Replaces the temporary `CallOp`-cloning maps with forward grouping by `(callee, metadata)` using `IfrtCallOpInfo`, followed by reverse iteration over `all_groups` through `CalleeSymbolManager::GetOrCloneCalleeForMutation(calls)`. This mutates a private, exclusively referenced `ModuleOp` in place with zero clones when all call sites share one configuration, bounds cloning to one per extra distinct variant with the earliest variant claiming the original name, and splits internal references inside outlined `ModuleOp`s into a private helper so internal callers remain unaffected by call-site metadata.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025243708

display_title: [IFRT] Add module-init registration for IFRT-internal ExecuteOptions::custom_options keys.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Add module-init registration for IFRT-internal ExecuteOptions::custom_options keys.

Keep `xla/python/ifrt/custom_options_util.{h,cc}` purely IFRT with a `RegisterIfrtInternalCustomOption` registration mechanism (modeled on `serdes.cc`, using an immortal `absl::Mutex`-guarded `absl::flat_hash_set<std::string>` with `CHECK` on duplicate registration, transparent `absl::string_view` lookup via `absl::ReaderMutexLock`, and leaf-lock ordering inside `AttributeMap::ForEach`).

- Move `"use_output_arena"` and `"call_location"` to a dedicated `alwayslink = True` leaf target `pjrt_ifrt:pjrt_custom_options` (`pjrt_custom_options.{h,cc}`), added to `pjrt_ifrt`'s `deps`. Alias `PjRtCompatibleLoadedExecutable::kCallLocation` and `kUseOutputArena` to these constants and use `kUseOutputArena` in `pjrt_executable.cc`.
- Move `"fill_all_statuses"` to a dedicated `alwayslink = True` leaf target `ifrt/ir:ifrt_ir_custom_options` (`ifrt_ir_custom_options.{h,cc}`), added to `ifrt_ir_program`'s `deps`. Alias `IfrtIRProgram::kFillAllStatuses` to this constant.
- Update `ToCustomOptionsMap` in `pjrt_executable.cc` to skip IFRT-internal keys during `ForEach` (avoiding copying internal values like traceback strings before erasing, and now also stripping `"fill_all_statuses"`).
- Add pure-IFRT unit tests in `custom_options_util_test.cc` (including key copy lifetime and duplicate registration death tests) and registration assertions in `pjrt_executable_impl_test_lib.cc` and `ifrt_ir_program_test.cc`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025238885

display_title: [IFRT IR] Adopt `CalleeSymbolManager` in `IfrtCallDedupPass`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Adopt `CalleeSymbolManager` in `IfrtCallDedupPass`

`IfrtCallDedupPass` maintained ad-hoc root-symbol counting, copy-on-write cloning, and `BumpPtrAllocator`-backed variant caching. When a private outlined module had internal `func.call` references, it cloned the entire module even for a sole caller, and when every call to a shared private callee was redirected to a cached specialized clone, the original symbol was left behind as dead IR.

Replaces the custom symbol-use tracking and cloning helpers with `CalleeSymbolManager`, migrates the specialized-callee cache from `llvm::DenseMap` + `llvm::BumpPtrAllocator` to `absl::flat_hash_map` with `absl::InlinedVector` keys, and erases newly unused private non-IFRT original root symbols via `EraseUnusedTrackedRootSymbols()` at pass exit. Sole-caller private outlined modules with internal references now split the unmutated callee into a private helper in place without cloning the enclosing module, and the pass fails cleanly on unregistered region-bearing ops in the root module. External declarations and multi-block callees continue to be skipped during upfront collection.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025229069

`IfrtCallDedupPass` maintained ad-hoc root-symbol counting, copy-on-write cloning, and `BumpPtrAllocator`-backed variant caching. When a private outlined module had internal `func.call` references, it cloned the entire module even for a sole caller, and when every call to a shared private callee was redirected to a cached specialized clone, the original symbol was left behind as dead IR.

Replaces the custom symbol-use tracking and cloning helpers with `CalleeSymbolManager`, migrates the specialized-callee cache from `llvm::DenseMap` + `llvm::BumpPtrAllocator` to `absl::flat_hash_map` with `absl::InlinedVector` keys, and erases newly unused private non-IFRT original root symbols via `EraseUnusedTrackedRootSymbols()` at pass exit. Sole-caller private outlined modules with internal references now split the unmutated callee into a private helper in place without cloning the enclosing module, and the pass fails cleanly on unregistered region-bearing ops in the root module. External declarations and multi-block callees continue to be skipped during upfront collection.

display_title: [XLA] Always use region analysis in copy removal

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Always use region analysis in copy removal

After speeding up region live range analysis in `CopyRemover`, the non region
fallback only leaves avoidable copies behind when unordered readers and in place
updates can be ordered by control dependencies.

Remove `use_region_based_live_range_analysis` from `CopyInsertion` and
`CopyRemover`, always fall back to region interference analysis when whole value
ordering is inconclusive, and deprecate the CPU and GPU
`xla_{cpu,gpu}_copy_insertion_use_region_analysis` flags as no ops. Delete the
now redundant `OrderPredecessorReadersBeforeInPlaceCopies` prepass, since region
analysis handles chained in place updates directly without adding control edges
to retained copies. Treat distinct values defined by the same multi output
instruction as interfering so separate in place outputs never share one buffer,
and preserve control dependencies on hoisted while loop calls in
`SmallWhileLoopHoistingPass`.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:copy_insertion_test` and
  `//xla/service/gpu:gpu_copy_insertion_test`: update copy count expectations,
  assert inserted control dependencies, and cover chained in place scatters and
  multi output in place custom calls.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/transforms:small_while_loop_hoisting_pass_test`: verifies
  control predecessors and successors transfer to the hoisted call.

Reverts 418ab7e0c7adcf7220b2ed6207f59b86cc9fce6a

name: CI
display_title: [IFRT IR] Adopt `CalleeSymbolManager` in `IfrtCopyConstantsPass`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Adopt `CalleeSymbolManager` in `IfrtCopyConstantsPass`

`IfrtCopyConstantsPass` previously counted only `ifrt.Call` references per callee and cloned with an ad-hoc helper. That caused the pass to mutate single-use public callees in place, corrupt private callees referenced by `func.call`, and mutate recursive outlined callees in place so internal recursive calls received constant-substituted bodies.

Replaces the custom reference counting and cloning logic with `CalleeSymbolManager`, tracking cloned constant ops via `RecordOpCreated`. Also adds a null guard when resolving producer callees in `FindHloProducer` and updates the `passes.td` description.

As part of adopting `CalleeSymbolManager::Create` and `GetCallee`, consumer `ifrt.Call` ops targeting external declarations, undefined callees, or callees nested deeper than one `ModuleOp` now emit an op error and fail the pass instead of being silently skipped (external and multi-block producer callees remain skipped). The pass also fails if root-scope or outlined-module symbol uses cannot be determined due to unregistered region-bearing ops.

`AtomProgramCompiler` currently exposes only `CompileXla` and `CompileMpmdReshard` methods that return `LoadedExecutable`s, coupling outlined atom program compilation to immediate device loading during MLIR pass execution.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Reject `Unknown` and `ShardGroup` `xla::HloSharding`s in `HloSharding` and `HloShardingSpec`

`xla::ifrt::HloSharding` and `xla::ifrt::HloShardingSpec` model concrete leaf array shardings, yet still accepted compiler-internal `Unknown` and `ShardGroup` `xla::HloSharding` instances during construction and `SerDes` deserialization (`Unknown` still `CHECK`-failed in `GetShardShape()` via `TiledDataRank()` and in `xla::HloSharding::ToNamedSharding()`, while `ShardGroup` is a compiler-only propagation annotation whose `shard_group_id == -1` form is silently dropped by `ToProto()`), and `HloShardingSpec::IndexDomains` skipped shape-rank validation on non-replicated subgroup shardings before calling `TileOffsetForDevice()`. In addition, `HloShardingSpecSerDes` lacked the `HloShardingV3` (`named_sharding`) serialization and deserialization guards present in `HloShardingSerDes`, and `HloShardingSerDes` inherited from `RTTIExtends<HloSharding, SerDes>` instead of `RTTIExtends<HloShardingSerDes, SerDes>`.

Reject `IsUnknown()` and any non-default `ShardGroup` (`!(GetShardGroup() == NotShardGroup())`) in `HloShardingSpec::CreateIfValid`, remove the now-unreachable `IsUnknown()` branches in `HloShardingSpec`, validate `shape.dims().size() == TiledDataRank()` before `HasNonReplicatedSubgroup()` in `HloShardingSpec::IndexDomains`, reject `HloShardingV3` (`named_sharding`) in `HloShardingSpecSerDes` via a shared `ContainsNamedSharding` helper, and fix `HloShardingSerDes`'s RTTI base class.

name: CI
display_title: [IFRT IR] Adopt `CalleeSymbolManager` in `IfrtDcePass`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Adopt `CalleeSymbolManager` in `IfrtDcePass`

`IfrtDcePass` previously maintained its own symbol-use counts and cloning logic that missed several edge cases: single-use public callees had their signatures mutated in place, shared live callees with pure dead ops were cloned unnecessarily before simplifying, recursive outlined callees were mutated without isolating internal `func.call` references, and dead-callee erasure was sensitive to reverse-walk order with no tracking of erased transfer/remap ops or unreachable `func.call` references.

Replaces the ad-hoc `ResolveCallee` and cloning logic with `CalleeSymbolManager`. Simplifies distinct defined callees (including shared and public callees) in place via `mlir::simplifyRegions` upfront so dead symbol references inside unreachable blocks are dropped before the reverse walk checks exclusivity.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Adopt `CalleeSymbolManager` in `IfrtCallDedupPass`

`IfrtCallDedupPass` maintained ad-hoc root-symbol counting, copy-on-write cloning, and `BumpPtrAllocator`-backed variant caching. When a private outlined module had internal `func.call` references, it cloned the entire module even for a sole caller, and when every call to a shared private callee was redirected to a cached specialized clone, the original symbol was left behind as dead IR.

Replaces the custom symbol-use tracking and cloning helpers with `CalleeSymbolManager`, migrates the specialized-callee cache from `llvm::DenseMap` + `llvm::BumpPtrAllocator` to `absl::flat_hash_map` with `absl::InlinedVector` keys, and erases newly unused private non-IFRT original root symbols via `EraseUnusedTrackedRootSymbols()` at pass exit. Sole-caller private outlined modules with internal references now split the unmutated callee into a private helper in place without cloning the enclosing module, and the pass fails cleanly on unregistered region-bearing ops in the root module. External declarations and multi-block callees continue to be skipped during upfront collection.

display_title: Add `is_mutable` parameter to `PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`.

head_commit.message:
Add `is_mutable` parameter to `PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`.

`CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` previously hardcoded
`is_mutable=false` when calling `ImportForeignMemory`. GPU ignored the flag,
while `CpuRawBuffer` honored it, so donating a view on PjRt CPU always
allocated a new output buffer instead of aliasing caller memory in place.
Unconditionally flipping `is_mutable` to `true` could surprise callers that
rely on read-only CPU views (such as NumPy or DLPack interop).

Thread an explicit `bool is_mutable` parameter through
`PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` (keeping the existing overload
defaulting to `is_mutable=false` for backwards compatibility),
`CommonPjRtClient`, `TfPjRtClient`, `PjRtCApiClient`, and the PJRT C API
v0.119 (`PJRT_Client_CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer_Args::is_mutable`). Callers
that want in-place donation on CPU can opt in with `is_mutable=true`, while
existing callers keep read-only CPU views by default.

Also avoid wrapping an empty `std::function<void()>` (`nullptr`) into a
non-empty `absl::AnyInvocable<void() &&>` in
`CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`, which previously threw
`std::bad_function_call` on buffer destruction when `on_delete_callback` was
null.

name: CI
display_title: Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

head_commit.message:
Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

When a JIT-compiled computation donates input buffers and fails before device execution begins (for example, due to a failed cross-host transfer or slice failure), surviving devices may still hold intact input buffers even though the caller's donated `jax.Array` handles have already been invalidated. Without runtime recovery, callers must restore donated state from a host snapshot or checkpoint.

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Fix inverted clamp evaluation order in collective offset matching

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Fix inverted clamp evaluation order in collective offset matching

In `collective_opt_utils.cc`, `EvaluateOffset` evaluated `kClamp` as `std::max(*lower, std::min(*inner, *upper))` instead of XLA HLO `std::min(*upper, std::max(*inner, *lower))`. When `lower` exceeded `upper`, `EvaluateOffset` returned `lower` while runtime execution returned `upper`. Offsets such as `subtract(id, clamp(0, id, -1))` evaluated to `id` instead of `id + 1`, causing `AllGatherSimplifier` and `MatchReduceScatter` to delete or misfuse cross device collectives. Evaluate `kClamp` as `std::min(*upper, std::max(*inner, *lower))`; valid non inverted clamp patterns and flags do not change.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Align variadic operand shardings in HandleReduceWindow

In `SpmdPartitioningVisitor::HandleReduceWindow`, each variadic input was resharded independently to its corresponding tuple output sharding before `CreateReduceWindow` ran locally without aligning the operands or resharding the result. When tuple elements have distinct device assignments or replication, partitions pair spatially mismatched input shards or fail shape and slice checks on tuple outputs. Select a single common tiled sharding across tuple elements, reshard variadic inputs to that sharding, slice each tuple element when `dynamic_slice_index_on_output` is set, and reshard the output to `hlo->sharding()`.

display_title: Ignore dynamic shape metadata prefix for static inputs and PadRealToStatic parameters in CheckBufferCompatibilities.

head_commit.message:
Ignore dynamic shape metadata prefix for static inputs and PadRealToStatic parameters in CheckBufferCompatibilities.

When `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::CheckBufferCompatibilities` validates parameter layouts on TPU, two valid dynamic-shape execution cases can have differing `dynamic_shape_metadata_prefix_bytes()` between the expected parameter shape and the actual input buffer: passing an unprefixed static buffer (`M(0)`) to an executable with a dynamic parameter (`M(1024)`), and passing a dynamic buffer with an in-buffer metadata prefix (`M(1024)`) to a `PadRealToStatic` parameter whose expected device shape has `M(0)`.

Extract `AreDynamicShapeMetadataPrefixesCompatible` and `ArePrefixDynamicParameterLayoutsCompatible` to accept unprefixed static buffers (`actual_shape.is_static()` with `actual_prefix == 0`) for dynamic parameters and prefixed dynamic buffers for `PadRealToStatic` parameters (`expected_prefix == 0`, where `CommonPjRtClient::PrepareArguments` slices the prefix off), while rejecting static buffers carrying a non-matching prefix (`M(n > 0)`) and guarding layoutless or non-array shapes. Also check `!actual_shape.has_layout() || actual_shape.layout().dynamic_shape_metadata_prefix_bytes() == 0` when deciding whether runtime bounds checks are external, validate dynamic buffer dimensions passed to static parameter dimensions, and reject negative runtime dimension sizes in `ReadDynamicShapeMetadata` and `CheckBufferCompatibilities`.

freed. Allocations outside tracked chunks (or spanning multiple chunks) fall

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Preserve sorted scatter indices when subtracting shard offsets

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Preserve sorted scatter indices when subtracting shard offsets

`PartitionScatterTrivialSlicedOperandDimensions` and `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` subtract `indices_min` in the original scatter index type while keeping `indices_are_sorted` true. On nonzero partitions, unsigned indices below `indices_min` and signed indices near the type minimum underflow to large positive values and break sortedness. When `indices_are_sorted` is true, `ClampSorted` clamps signed indices at `-1` and converts unsigned indices to `S32` or `S64` after capping at the signed maximum. Existing valid programs are unchanged.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Fix inverted clamp evaluation order in collective offset matching

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Fix inverted clamp evaluation order in collective offset matching

In `collective_opt_utils.cc`, `EvaluateOffset` evaluated `kClamp` as `std::max(*lower, std::min(*inner, *upper))` instead of XLA HLO `std::min(*upper, std::max(*inner, *lower))`. When `lower` exceeded `upper`, `EvaluateOffset` returned `lower` while runtime execution returned `upper`. Offsets such as `subtract(id, clamp(0, id, -1))` evaluated to `id` instead of `id + 1`, causing `AllGatherSimplifier` and `MatchReduceScatter` to delete or misfuse cross device collectives. Evaluate `kClamp` as `std::min(*upper, std::max(*inner, *lower))`; valid non inverted clamp patterns and flags do not change.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Add missing root and control-dependency checks in ConditionalCodeMotion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add missing root and control-dependency checks in ConditionalCodeMotion.

ConditionalCodeMotion missed several soundness checks around parent roots and control dependencies:
1) Moving instructions with control dependencies across branch boundaries dropped their control edges (and failed RemoveInstruction on the original op), and MoveInstructionOut unconditionally removed every existing GTE user of the conditional even if one had control dependencies.
2) BoundariesToMoveInOrOut seeded move-out and move-user-in even when the conditional itself was the parent ROOT, allowing its output shape or root value to be mutated.
3) RestructureConditionalInstruction skipped redirecting pre-existing users of the conditional to new_tuple when the conditional was ROOT, leaving ConvertSpecialMove with duplicate GTEs at the same index.
4) WorthHoisting allowed non-tuple ROOT operands to be moved into branches, and MoveOperandIntoBranch deleted moved operands via user_count() == 0 instead of IsDead(), crashing when a ROOT operand or replicated ROOT broadcast lost its last user.

Reject instructions with control dependencies in WorthHoisting, broadcast replication, MoveInstructionOut user checks, and ConvertSpecialMove; skip seeding branch-out/user-in for a ROOT conditional; redirect all pre-existing users in RestructureConditionalInstruction regardless of whether the conditional is ROOT; and skip ROOT operands in WorthHoisting while guarding MoveOperandIntoBranch removal with IsDead().

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025895596

display_title: [XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

MoveUserInstructionsIn previously tried to predict whether tuple_use would become dead using only tuple_use->user_count() == 1, eagerly dropping its tuple slot and shifting later GTE indices before dead instructions were removed. That silently miscompiled when a sibling GTE read the same tuple_index, corrupted a live ROOT GTE before RunImpl crashed trying to remove it via user_count() == 0, and missed compacting multi-user GTEs whose consumers all moved in.

Always append moved-in results in MoveUserInstructionsIn while preserving existing slots, shardings, and OriginalValue entries in place, guard RunImpl removals with IsDead() and IsSafelyRemovable(), and compact unused branch outputs once in RemoveUnusedBranchOutputs from the actual surviving GTE users (updating tuple shardings and remapping kept OriginalValue subtrees via CopyOriginalValue).

display_title: Ignore dynamic shape metadata prefix for static inputs and PadRealToStatic parameters in CheckBufferCompatibilities.

head_commit.message:
Ignore dynamic shape metadata prefix for static inputs and PadRealToStatic parameters in CheckBufferCompatibilities.

When `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::CheckBufferCompatibilities` validates parameter layouts on TPU, two valid dynamic-shape execution cases can have differing `dynamic_shape_metadata_prefix_bytes()` between the expected parameter shape and the actual input buffer: passing an unprefixed static buffer (`M(0)`) to an executable with a dynamic parameter (`M(1024)`), and passing a dynamic buffer with an in-buffer metadata prefix (`M(1024)`) to a `PadRealToStatic` parameter whose expected device shape has `M(0)`.

Extract `AreDynamicShapeMetadataPrefixesCompatible` and `ArePrefixDynamicParameterLayoutsCompatible` to accept unprefixed static buffers (`actual_shape.is_static()` with `actual_prefix == 0`) for dynamic parameters and prefixed dynamic buffers for `PadRealToStatic` parameters (`expected_prefix == 0`, where `CommonPjRtClient::PrepareArguments` slices the prefix off), while rejecting static buffers carrying a non-matching prefix (`M(n > 0)`) and guarding layoutless or non-array shapes. Also check `!actual_shape.has_layout() || actual_shape.layout().dynamic_shape_metadata_prefix_bytes() == 0` when deciding whether runtime bounds checks are external, validate dynamic buffer dimensions passed to static parameter dimensions, and reject negative runtime dimension sizes in `ReadDynamicShapeMetadata` and `CheckBufferCompatibilities`.

head_commit.message:
Make PjRt CPU views mutable in CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer.

`CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` passed `is_mutable=false` to
`ImportForeignMemory`. GPU ignored this flag, while `CpuRawBuffer` honored it.
Donating a view on PjRt CPU therefore allocated a new output buffer instead of
aliasing caller memory in place. The `CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` contract permits
mutation on donation.

Pass `is_mutable=true` in `CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` so
donated CPU views alias caller memory in place.

Update `PartitioningOpInterface::resolvePermutationFactors` and

communication for custom-rule or ruleless ops while allocating unique channel

- **Early dispatch**: Invoke `PartitioningOpInterface::resolvePermutationFactors`
  before the `!rule || rule.isCustom()` and permutation-factor filters, falling
  through to generic handling on `std::nullopt`.

display_title: [XLA] Preserve control dependencies when stitching submodules

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve control dependencies when stitching submodules

`HloModuleStitcher` replaced `_xla_multi_module_call` custom calls with `kCall`
instructions and deleted the original custom call without moving or dropping its
control dependencies. When an optimization pass such as `CopyInsertion` orders
another instruction before or after the custom call, `RemoveInstruction` fails
its `IsSafelyRemovable` check.

Transfer control predecessors to the stitched `kCall`, transfer control
successors to its replacement (the layout reconciling `kCopy` when present,
otherwise the `kCall`), and drop the original custom call's control edges before
removal.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:hlo_module_stitcher_test`: verifies control predecessors
  and successors are preserved with and without a result layout copy.

display_title: [IFRT] Introduce `IfrtIrExecutable` and compile-only `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Introduce `IfrtIrExecutable` and compile-only `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile`

`IfrtIrProgramCompiler` currently implements `CompileAndLoad`, while `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile(program, topology, options)` has no compiled `Executable` representation for holding a lowered IFRT IR module and its unloaded atom programs prior to `Client::Load`.

Introduce `IfrtIrExecutable` (`RTTIExtends<IfrtIrExecutable, Executable>`) to own the lowered `IfrtIRProgram` in a dedicated `MLIRContext` (parsing per-load `MLIRContext` instances from pre-serialized MLIR bytecode in `CreateCompiledIfrtIrProgram` so concurrent `Client::Load` calls do not mutate the shared `MLIRContext`), expose its compiled atom programs and metadata queries, and wire `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile` to `IfrtIrExecutable::Create`. Target device resolution continues to use the compiler's `Client*` and `IfrtIRCompileOptions::device_assignments`, and `Client::Load` support for `IfrtIrExecutable` lands in a follow-up change.

name: CI
display_title: [IFRT] Validate matching rank and non-overflowing upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate matching rank and non-overflowing upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

`IndexDomain` permitted `origin` and `shape` with mismatched ranks and allowed `origin[i] + shape.dims()[i]` to exceed `INT64_MAX`, forcing `Intersect` and `Contains` to repeat per-operand rank checks while leaving `origin[i] + shape[i]` upper-bound calculations vulnerable to signed `int64_t` overflow. In addition, `IndexDomain(Shape shape)` passed both `Index::Zeros(shape.dims().size())` and `std::move(shape)` in the same delegating constructor call, relying on unspecified C++ argument evaluation order.

Add `IndexDomain::Create` to validate `origin.elements().size() == shape.dims().size()` and non-overflowing `origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]` upper bounds, delegate `IndexDomain(origin, shape)` (via `CHECK_OK`) and `IndexDomain::FromProto` to `IndexDomain::Create`, initialize `origin_` and `shape_` directly in `IndexDomain(Shape shape)`, and route `operator+=` / `operator-=` through `operator+` / `operator-` so offset mutations preserve upper-bound validity.

display_title: PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

head_commit.message:
PR #52878: [ROCM] Wire MORI ragged-all-to-all and all-gather through the GXL hook, add async start/done stubs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52878

## Summary

This change makes the MORI GPU collectives backend serve XLA's GXL
ragged-all-to-all / all-gather hook and adds async start/done support to the
MORI communicator, so ragged-all-to-all and other MORI collectives can be
issued on an async stream and overlapped by the latency-hiding scheduler.

It is gated behind the existing `--xla_gpu_enable_gxl_ragged_all_to_all` flag
and only takes effect when the collectives implementation is MORI
(`--xla_gpu_collectives_implementation=mori`); the default NCCL/RCCL path is
unchanged.

## Motivation

`RaggedAllToAllThunk` previously only had the symmetric-memory and peer-access
kernel strategies. MORI already implements a fast SDMA-push ragged-all-to-all
in the `CollectivesFacade`, but there was no way for the thunk to call into it.
I decided to reuse already existing `GxlCommunicator` interface (`RunAllGatherGxl`,
`RunRaggedAllToAllGxl`) for exactly this purpose, reached via
`GpuCommunicator::gxl_communicator()`. This PR implements that hook for MORI and
teaches the ragged-all-to-all thunk to delegate to it.

This way, we **do not need to add anything specific** to RaggedAllToAllThunk which is already quite complex.
There are just _two general fixes_ in RaggedAllToAllThunk related to GXL communicator handling.

## What changed

### GXL hook (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`)

- `MoriCommunicator` now overrides `gxl_communicator()` and owns a nested
  `GxlAdapter` (a `GxlCommunicator` holding a back-pointer to the communicator).
  Using a member adapter rather than multiple inheritance keeps the
  `GpuCommunicator`/`GxlCommunicator` hierarchies separate.
- `GxlAdapter::RunAllGatherGxl` forwards to `LaunchAllGather`;
  `RunRaggedAllToAllGxl` forwards to the new `LaunchRaggedAllToAll`.

### Ragged-all-to-all thunk (`ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc`)

- `Initialize`: when `enable_gxl` is set and the clique's communicator exposes a
  GXL communicator, return early — the GXL path runs the whole op, so no kernel
  or NCCL-fallback state is allocated (kernel strategy stays `kNone`).
- `Record`: under the same condition, delegate to `CollectiveThunk::Record`,
  which traces `RunCollective` and dispatches to the GXL communicator.

### Async start/done (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`, `mori_kernels.h`)

- Added `SetAsync(bool)` / `AsyncDone(executor)` and an internal
  `LaunchOrDefer` helper. These is a preparation for MORI async collectives support, **not wired yet**.
- Removed the old `Execute` wrapper; the `Launch*` methods are called directly.

### Build / misc

- Renamed the MORI facade namespace usages from `mori::collective` to
  `mori::ccl` to match the repinned MORI headers.

### MORI repin (`third_party/roc_mori/workspace.bzl`)

- Repinned `@roc_mori` to MORI tag `xla-pin-20261112`
  (commit `d50338eb5f45d4338ee64ef27fa7f22a71638b9f`) with the matching archive
  `sha256`.

## Testing

- `RaggedAllToAll_2GPUs_CommandBuffer/async_nccl_fallback_peer` passes,
  exercising the async + command-buffer path end-to-end through the MORI GXL
  hook.
- Verified on a MaxText Mixtral-8x7b MoE run (expert-parallel, EP=8) that the
  MORI ragged-all-to-all kernel is selected and produces correct results; the
  collective runs at the standalone benchmark's bandwidth when ranks arrive
  together.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Assign async D2D copies to a single dedicated stream.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Assign async D2D copies to a single dedicated stream.

***Problem:*** Asynchronous device-to-device copy-start instructions and dynamic-slice copy fusions fall back to the general compute stream pool, round-robining device-to-device memory copies across multiple compute streams and contending with asynchronous compute kernels.

***Solution:*** Classify unannotated device-to-device copy-start and dynamic-slice copy fusion-start scopes as kMemcpyD2D when dedicated memcpy streams are enabled and assign them to a single shared ComputationStreamId disjoint from active compute streams.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

Constructing an `xla::ifrt::Shape` deferred negative-dimension checks to `Shape::num_elements()` and permitted dimensions whose total element count overflowed `int64_t` or exceeded what bit-size and byte-size calculations could represent. Callers computing `shape.num_elements() * dtype.bit_size()` or `shape.num_elements() * dtype.byte_size()` could silently wrap signed `int64_t` unless every backend and utility repeated its own checked multiplication.

Add `Shape::Create` to validate non-negative dimensions and that the product of non-zero dimensions fits within `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (`INT64_MAX / 128`, accommodating elements up to 128 bits), returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` on invalid dimensions, and delegate `Shape`'s constructor (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Shape::FromProto` to `Shape::Create`. Enforce the same `Shape::kMaxNumElements` bound in `IfrtArrayType::verify`, `VifrtArrayV1Type::verify`, and `PjRtExecutable` shape conversions, remove `Shape::NumElements()`, drop redundant downstream negative-dimension and byte-size overflow checks, and update IFRT unit tests that constructed `Shape` with negative dimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in GemmFusion

GemmFusion copied only the dot's metadata onto the Triton fusion. When the
fused output was not a computation root, ReplaceInstruction still copied its
frontend attributes onto the replacement, but when it was the root (e.g. a jit

`_scheduling_group_id`, were dropped.

Derive the fusion, and the bitcast that replaces the dot when the shapes
differ, from the dot, so they keep its metadata and frontend attributes.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve control dependencies when stitching submodules

`HloModuleStitcher` replaced `_xla_multi_module_call` custom calls with `kCall`
instructions and deleted the original custom call without moving or dropping its
control dependencies. When an optimization pass such as `CopyInsertion` orders
another instruction before or after the custom call, `RemoveInstruction` fails
its `IsSafelyRemovable` check.

Transfer control predecessors to the stitched `kCall`, transfer control
successors to its replacement (the layout reconciling `kCopy` when present,
otherwise the `kCall`), and drop the original custom call's control edges before
removal.

  and successors are preserved with and without a result layout copy.

display_title: [IFRT] Introduce `IfrtIrExecutable` and compile-only `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Introduce `IfrtIrExecutable` and compile-only `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile`

`IfrtIrProgramCompiler` currently implements `CompileAndLoad`, while `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile(program, topology, options)` has no compiled `Executable` representation for holding a lowered IFRT IR module and its unloaded atom programs prior to `Client::Load`.

Introduce `IfrtIrExecutable` (`RTTIExtends<IfrtIrExecutable, Executable>`) to own the lowered `IfrtIRProgram` in a dedicated `MLIRContext` (parsing per-load `MLIRContext` instances from pre-serialized MLIR bytecode in `CreateCompiledIfrtIrProgram` so concurrent `Client::Load` calls do not mutate the shared `MLIRContext`), expose its compiled atom programs and metadata queries, and wire `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile` to `IfrtIrExecutable::Create`. Target device resolution continues to use the compiler's `Client*` and `IfrtIRCompileOptions::device_assignments`, and `Client::Load` support for `IfrtIrExecutable` lands in a follow-up change.

name: CI
display_title: Recompute dynamic-update-slice update tiling in HostOffloadLegalize.

head_commit.message:
Recompute dynamic-update-slice update tiling in HostOffloadLegalize.

When `HostOffloadLegalize` sinks a layout-changing `copy` past a
`dynamic-update-slice`, it converts the update to the buffer's layout on device
and gives the update's `MoveToHost` annotation the buffer's `Layout`. The tiles
in that layout were chosen for the full buffer, so an update that is smaller in
the 2nd-minor dimension kept stale tiles.

Call `HloModulePass::UpdateLayout` on the update's `MoveToHost` shape, so the
annotation and the device-side copy created from it get tiling that matches the
update's dimensions.

name: CI
display_title: Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

head_commit.message:
Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

When a JIT-compiled computation donates input buffers and fails before device execution begins (for example, due to a failed cross-host transfer or slice failure), surviving devices may still hold intact input buffers even though the caller's donated `jax.Array` handles have already been invalidated. Without runtime recovery, callers must restore donated state from a host snapshot or checkpoint.

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

display_title: [XLA] Always use region analysis in copy removal

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Always use region analysis in copy removal

After speeding up region live range analysis in `CopyRemover`, the non region
fallback only leaves avoidable copies behind when unordered readers and in place
updates can be ordered by control dependencies.

Remove `use_region_based_live_range_analysis` from `CopyInsertion` and
`CopyRemover`, always fall back to region interference analysis when whole value
ordering is inconclusive, and deprecate the CPU and GPU
`xla_{cpu,gpu}_copy_insertion_use_region_analysis` flags as no ops. Delete the
now redundant `OrderPredecessorReadersBeforeInPlaceCopies` prepass, since region
analysis handles chained in place updates directly without adding control edges
to retained copies. Treat distinct values defined by the same multi output
instruction as interfering so separate in place outputs never share one buffer,
and preserve control dependencies on hoisted while loop calls in
`SmallWhileLoopHoistingPass`.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:copy_insertion_test` and
  `//xla/service/gpu:gpu_copy_insertion_test`: update copy count expectations,
  assert inserted control dependencies, and cover chained in place scatters and
  multi output in place custom calls.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/transforms:small_while_loop_hoisting_pass_test`: verifies
  control predecessors and successors transfer to the hoisted call.

Reverts 418ab7e0c7adcf7220b2ed6207f59b86cc9fce6a

name: CI
display_title: PR #3040: Support f16- and bf16-based complex types

head_commit.message:
PR #3040: Support f16- and bf16-based complex types

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/stablehlo/pull/3040

Implements RFC #2993 by extending StableHLO's supported complex component types from {f32, f64} to {f16, bf16, f32, f64}.

- Introduces a shared, closed-set component predicate for ODS constraints, stablehlo.complex operands, and RFFT type inference.
- Bumps the current version to 1.27.0 and adds target-version-aware VHLO type constraints while retaining ComplexV1 and its existing encoding. Low-precision complex types cannot be serialized to earlier targets; existing f32/f64 complex type compatibility is preserved.
- Checks nested VHLO types, including futures, quantized-type parameters, and region block arguments.
- Updates the specification and adds verifier, inference, round-trip, downgrade, and versioned bytecode coverage.

CHLO's asin, acos, asinh, acosh, atanh, and atan retain verifier rejection of `complex<f16>` because their existing numerical decompositions do not support it reliably. Real f16 and `complex<bf16>`, `complex<f32>`, and `complex<f64>` remain accepted. broadcast_complex supports both new component types. The mathematical decomposition kernels are unchanged.

This PR covers StableHLO type validity and portable serialization. XLA/HLO support, the StableHLO-to-XLA bridge, backend execution, and reference-interpreter execution for the new complex types remain follow-up work.

Testing: 292 lit tests under stablehlo/tests passed with assertions enabled, including:

- StableHLO verifier and type-inference coverage, with all four FFT modes for both f16 and bf16.
- Nested-type downgrade rejection and CHLO constraint-boundary checks.
- The 1.27.0 serialization fixture and byte-exact round trips.
- Existing mathematical and historical compatibility regressions.

Related: #1794.

display_title: Recompute dynamic-update-slice update tiling in HostOffloadLegalize.

head_commit.message:
Recompute dynamic-update-slice update tiling in HostOffloadLegalize.

When `HostOffloadLegalize` sinks a layout-changing `copy` past a
`dynamic-update-slice`, it converts the update to the buffer's layout on device
and gives the update's `MoveToHost` annotation the buffer's `Layout`. The tiles
in that layout were chosen for the full buffer, so an update that is smaller in
the 2nd-minor dimension kept stale tiles.

Call `HloModulePass::UpdateLayout` on the update's `MoveToHost` shape, so the
annotation and the device-side copy created from it get tiling that matches the
update's dimensions.

display_title: PR #48502: [ROCm] Add ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration into the ROCm tracer (PR2)

head_commit.message:
PR #48502: [ROCm] Add ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration into the ROCm tracer (PR2)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48502

This is the second among three PRs.

We add a parser for the `gpu_*` keys in `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration`. Nothing calls it yet; #48503 wires it into GpuTracer.

The CUPTI parser stops at the first bad key and fails `Start()`. `ProfilerController` then never calls `CollectData()`, so the user loses the GPU trace and the reason is only in the log. This one applies every valid key and returns the problems as errors and warnings; `AppendOptionDiagnostics` writes them to `XSpace.errors`/`warnings` and the log.

What each key does on ROCm:

- `gpu_max_callback_api_events`, `gpu_max_annotation_strings`: applied. A negative value is an error; anything above 1e9 is clamped with a warning. Callback events = 0 means "no limit" on CUDA, so here it becomes 1e9 with a warning (passed through, 0 would drop the whole trace). Annotation strings = 0 is applied and warns that kernels will have no op names.
- `gpu_max_activity_api_events`: stored, but always warns that it isn't enforced. The collector only counts HIP_API activity events, and every activity record is HIP_OPS.
- `gpu_num_chips_to_profile_per_task`: 0 or more than the GPU count means all GPUs, as on CUDA. Negative is an error. A smaller K is applied with a warning: all GPUs are still traced, and afterwards only K consecutive device ids are kept, starting at the lowest one that recorded an event.
- The CUPTI-only keys (NVTX, aggregated tracing, graph trace, PM sampling) and `gpu_dump_graph_node_mapping`: type-checked, then a "no effect on ROCm" warning. No warning when the value is what ROCm does anyway, e.g. `gpu_enable_nvtx_tracking=true`.
- Any other `gpu_*` key is an error. Keys without the `gpu_` prefix are left alone, since other profiler components read the same map.

Two smaller changes. The ROCm key list is a hand copy of CUPTI's, so `cupti_tracer_options_utils.cc` gets a comment (no code change), and `EveryCuptiKeyIsRecognized` reads that file and fails if a CUPTI key is missing here. The 1e9 cap is now `kMaxRocmTraceEvents` in `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, shared with `--xla_gpu_rocm_max_trace_events`, with a `static_assert` that it fits the collector's `int` counters.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

🧪 Unit Tests:

`rocm_tracer_options_utils_test` adds 30 host-only cases (no GPU needed). At `f8eeb882cf` on MI355X with `--config=rocm_ci_hermetic` (TheRock 10.0.0), it passes, and so do `rocm_tracer_utils_test`, `rocm_tracer_test` and `rocm_collector_test`.

[ROCm profiler] Add rocm_tracer_options_utils

Second of three changes to support ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration
in the ROCm tracer. Adds the parser; nothing calls it yet.

UpdateRocmTracerOptionsFromProfilerOptions applies the gpu_* keys over
the caller's defaults and returns every problem as an error or warning,
instead of stopping at the first one as CUPTI does.
AppendOptionDiagnostics writes them to XSpace.errors/warnings and the
log.

- Event and annotation limits: a negative value is an error. For the two
  event limits, 0 means no limit, as on CUDA; passed through, it would
  empty the trace. gpu_max_annotation_strings = 0 retains none, as on
  CUDA, and draws a warning. gpu_max_activity_api_events is stored but
  not enforced yet, because the collector only counts HIP_API activity
  events; a warning says so.
- gpu_num_chips_to_profile_per_task: 0 or more than the device count
  means every GPU, as on CUDA. A negative value is an error. A smaller
  value draws a warning that every GPU is still traced.
- Keys CUPTI implements but ROCm does not draw a "not implemented"
  warning, whatever their value.
- Unknown gpu_* keys are errors. Other keys belong to other profiler
  components and are ignored.

RocmTraceCollectorImpl counts events in uint64_t guarded by
event_maps_mutex_, which every access already holds, instead of
std::atomic<int>, so a limit above INT_MAX no longer wraps the counter.

EveryCuptiKeyIsRecognized keeps the two key lists in sync: it reads the
CUPTI parser's source and fails if ROCm neither applies nor warns about
one of its keys. The RocmTraceCollectorOptions comments drop "if -1, no
limit".

Tests: rocm_tracer_options_utils_test, 25 host-only cases.

Merging this change closes #48502

head_commit.message:
Add `GpuDmaBufCache` for suballocator chunk-level Linux dma-buf fd caching.

Caching exported dma-buf fds per suballocator chunk avoids per-buffer driver
export overhead and file descriptor exhaustion under high concurrency, while
`free_visitor` invalidation ensures fds are closed before the backing memory is
freed. Allocations outside tracked chunks (or spanning multiple chunks) fall
back to an uncached RAII export.

display_title: PR #3040: Support f16- and bf16-based complex types

head_commit.message:
PR #3040: Support f16- and bf16-based complex types

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/stablehlo/pull/3040

Implements RFC #2993 by extending StableHLO's supported complex component types from {f32, f64} to {f16, bf16, f32, f64}.

- Introduces a shared, closed-set component predicate for ODS constraints, stablehlo.complex operands, and RFFT type inference.
- Bumps the current version to 1.27.0 and adds target-version-aware VHLO type constraints while retaining ComplexV1 and its existing encoding. Low-precision complex types cannot be serialized to earlier targets; existing f32/f64 complex type compatibility is preserved.
- Checks nested VHLO types, including futures, quantized-type parameters, and region block arguments.
- Updates the specification and adds verifier, inference, round-trip, downgrade, and versioned bytecode coverage.

CHLO's asin, acos, asinh, acosh, atanh, and atan retain verifier rejection of `complex<f16>` because their existing numerical decompositions do not support it reliably. Real f16 and `complex<bf16>`, `complex<f32>`, and `complex<f64>` remain accepted. broadcast_complex supports both new component types. The mathematical decomposition kernels are unchanged.

This PR covers StableHLO type validity and portable serialization. XLA/HLO support, the StableHLO-to-XLA bridge, backend execution, and reference-interpreter execution for the new complex types remain follow-up work.

Testing: 292 lit tests under stablehlo/tests passed with assertions enabled, including:

- StableHLO verifier and type-inference coverage, with all four FFT modes for both f16 and bf16.
- Nested-type downgrade rejection and CHLO constraint-boundary checks.
- The 1.27.0 serialization fixture and byte-exact round trips.
- Existing mathematical and historical compatibility regressions.

Related: #1794.

Donate PjRt-IFRT executable inputs according to donation intent.

`LoadedExecutable::GetDonatableInputIndices()` reports parameter donation intent (`jax.buffer_donor` and `tf.aliasing_output`), whereas XLA compilation may leave a donor unaliased when no compatible output buffer exists. display_title: [IFRT] Disallow V3 `NamedSharding` and validate `SingleDevice` and tile-divisor invariants in `HloShardingSpec`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate `SingleDevice` and V3 `NamedSharding` invariants in `HloShardingSpec`

`HloShardingSpec` accepted negative `SingleDevice` device IDs and non-tiled V3 `NamedSharding`s whose explicit mesh size differed from `num_shards`, deferred checking `num_shards % NumTiles() == 0` until query time, and called `tile_assignment()` in `UniqueIndexDomains` and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex` (which `CHECK`-fails on V3 `NamedSharding`s).

Validate non-negative `SingleDevice` device IDs, `num_shards % NumTiles() == 0`, and non-empty V3 `NamedSharding` mesh sizes upfront in `HloShardingSpec::CreateIfValid`, and use `device_assignment()` in `UniqueIndexDomains` and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`.

display_title: [XLA] Always use region analysis in copy removal

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Always use region analysis in copy removal

After speeding up region live range analysis in `CopyRemover`, the non region
fallback only leaves avoidable copies behind when unordered readers and in place
updates can be ordered by control dependencies.

Remove `use_region_based_live_range_analysis` from `CopyInsertion` and
`CopyRemover`, always fall back to region interference analysis when whole value
ordering is inconclusive, and deprecate the CPU and GPU
`xla_{cpu,gpu}_copy_insertion_use_region_analysis` flags as no ops. Delete the
now redundant `OrderPredecessorReadersBeforeInPlaceCopies` prepass, since region
analysis handles chained in place updates directly without adding control edges
to retained copies. Treat distinct values defined by the same multi output
instruction as interfering so separate in place outputs never share one buffer,
and preserve control dependencies on hoisted while loop calls in
`SmallWhileLoopHoistingPass`.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:copy_insertion_test` and
  `//xla/service/gpu:gpu_copy_insertion_test`: update copy count expectations,
  assert inserted control dependencies, and cover chained in place scatters and
  multi output in place custom calls.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/transforms:small_while_loop_hoisting_pass_test`: verifies
  control predecessors and successors transfer to the hoisted call.

Reverts 418ab7e0c7adcf7220b2ed6207f59b86cc9fce6a

name: CI
display_title: PR #3040: Support f16- and bf16-based complex types

head_commit.message:
PR #3040: Support f16- and bf16-based complex types

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/stablehlo/pull/3040

Implements RFC #2993 by extending StableHLO's supported complex component types from {f32, f64} to {f16, bf16, f32, f64}.

- Introduces a shared, closed-set component predicate for ODS constraints, stablehlo.complex operands, and RFFT type inference.
- Bumps the current version to 1.27.0 and adds target-version-aware VHLO type constraints while retaining ComplexV1 and its existing encoding. Low-precision complex types cannot be serialized to earlier targets; existing f32/f64 complex type compatibility is preserved.
- Checks nested VHLO types, including futures, quantized-type parameters, and region block arguments.
- Updates the specification and adds verifier, inference, round-trip, downgrade, and versioned bytecode coverage.

CHLO's asin, acos, asinh, acosh, atanh, and atan retain verifier rejection of `complex<f16>` because their existing numerical decompositions do not support it reliably. Real f16 and `complex<bf16>`, `complex<f32>`, and `complex<f64>` remain accepted. broadcast_complex supports both new component types. The mathematical decomposition kernels are unchanged.

This PR covers StableHLO type validity and portable serialization. XLA/HLO support, the StableHLO-to-XLA bridge, backend execution, and reference-interpreter execution for the new complex types remain follow-up work.

Testing: 292 lit tests under stablehlo/tests passed with assertions enabled, including:

- StableHLO verifier and type-inference coverage, with all four FFT modes for both f16 and bf16.
- Nested-type downgrade rejection and CHLO constraint-boundary checks.
- The 1.27.0 serialization fixture and byte-exact round trips.
- Existing mathematical and historical compatibility regressions.

Related: #1794.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

Constructing an `xla::ifrt::Shape` deferred negative-dimension checks to `Shape::num_elements()` and permitted dimensions whose total element count overflowed `int64_t` or exceeded what bit-size and byte-size calculations could represent. Callers computing `shape.num_elements() * dtype.bit_size()` or `shape.num_elements() * dtype.byte_size()` could silently wrap signed `int64_t` unless every backend and utility repeated its own checked multiplication.

Add `Shape::Create` to validate non-negative dimensions and that the product of non-zero dimensions fits within `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (`INT64_MAX / 128`, accommodating elements up to 128 bits), returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` on invalid dimensions, and delegate `Shape`'s constructor (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Shape::FromProto` to `Shape::Create`. Enforce the same `Shape::kMaxNumElements` bound in `IfrtArrayType::verify`, `VifrtArrayV1Type::verify`, and `PjRtExecutable` shape conversions, remove `Shape::NumElements()`, drop redundant downstream negative-dimension and byte-size overflow checks, and update IFRT unit tests that constructed `Shape` with negative dimensions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1021496910

name: CI
display_title: [GPU][ROCm] Enable RCCL symmetric memory on ROCm

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Enable RCCL symmetric memory on ROCm

Implement and enable RCCL symmetric-memory support so that one-shot
symmetric-memory collective kernels work on ROCm/RCCL, bringing the ROCm
path closer to parity with the CUDA/NCCL implementation.

RcclSymmetricMemory:
- Implement peer_addr() using ncclGetPeerDevicePointer (ROCm/RCCL 10.0+),
  returning FailedPrecondition when a peer is not load/store accessible
  and Unimplemented on older toolkits.
- Require NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE >= 1 before registering a window. On ROCm the
  variable defaults to 0, which leaves comm->symmetricSupport disabled and
  makes ncclCommWindowRegister(NCCL_WIN_COLL_SYMMETRIC) silently downgrade
  to a non-symmetric window. The variable is read once per process, like
  RCCL's own ncclCuMemEnable().
- Validate the registered window with an ncclGetPeerDevicePointer probe:
  RCCL can return ncclSuccess while downgrading to a non-symmetric window,
  which would later crash inside RCCL ("Could not find communicator
  matching window"). Deregister and fail cleanly instead.
- Annotate registration failures with a hint about the allocator flags
  required for VMM-backed buffers.
- Plumb the symmetric_window flag through to the window registration
  flags (NCCL_WIN_COLL_SYMMETRIC vs NCCL_WIN_DEFAULT).

RcclCommunicator: run symmetric window registration on the communicator's
owning executor, and pass that executor to RcclSymmetricMemory so that
deregistration runs on the same thread, as RCCL requires.

IsLsaPossible: report LSA support on ROCm when the HIP runtime is >= 7.15
(shipped by ROCm 10.0, which is the first release with the RCCL window
APIs) and NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE >= 1.

Tests: gate the multi-process one-shot collective e2e tests on HIP runtime
7.15+, and update rccl_symmetric_memory_test to skip when a single-rank
communicator cannot back an LSA window, plus cover NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE
parsing through internal::NcclCuMemEnabledStatus.

display_title: [XLA] Return std::nullopt from PatternMatchParseWhileLoop for infinite and constant-condition loops

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Return std::nullopt from PatternMatchParseWhileLoop for infinite and constant-condition loops

`PatternMatchParseWhileLoop` previously returned `ParsedStaticWhileLoop` with `-1` sentinels (`trip_count = -1` in `HandleNoopLoopCondition` for infinite boolean-flag loops, and `induction_var_index = -1` with `trip_count = -1` or `0` in `HandleStaticLoopComparison` for constant comparisons). Callers such as `TryParseAndEvaluateWhileInductionVar` and `WhileLoopAnalysis::ComputeLoopStatistics` only checked `is_dynamic()` before indexing `while_hlo->shape().tuple_shapes(-1)`, triggering an out-of-bounds read and AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free (#49823).

Return `std::nullopt` from `PatternMatchParseWhileLoop` for infinite boolean-flag loops and constant-comparison conditions (and bounds-check `tuple_index` in `EvaluateWhileLoopParamInitValue`), `CHECK` the non-negative `trip_count` and valid `induction_var_index` invariants in `HloEvaluator`, and compute `induction_var_init_value + trip_count * step_size` in `uint64_t` in `TryParseAndEvaluateWhileInductionVar` to avoid signed integer overflow matching `HandleWhile`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025640141

display_title: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Autotuner support (PR 7/8)

head_commit.message:
[XTile][RaggedDot] Autotuner support

Add autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions, which now carry the
generic kTritonFusionKind rather than the legacy kTritonGemmFusionKind.

Autotuner (triton.cc / triton.h):
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig
  search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting,
  Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a
  BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported(): claim kTritonFusionKind fusions that contain a kRaggedDot,
  before the GEMM-fusion kind check.  Only those: all other generic Triton
  fusions belong to BlockLevelEmitterBackend.  This replaces the previous
  branch, which was unreachable behind the kind check and relied on the
  now-removed xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tiling_propagation debug option.
- BlockLevelEmitterBackend::IsSupported(): skip fusions containing a
  kRaggedDot so that it and TritonBackend cannot both claim them when
  xla_gpu_experimental_all_fusions_with_triton is set.

Pass wiring:
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.
- config_assigner_pass: route ragged-dot Triton fusions to
  ShouldAssignConfigToGemmFusion().  Without this they fall through to
  generic fusion autotuning, which rejects every kCustom fusion, so no
  config would ever be assigned.  They always carry a default
  BlockLevelFusionConfig from GemmRewriter, hence no "already has a
  config" check.
- config_assigner_pass: drop the register-spilling carve-out for
  ragged-dot; kTritonFusionKind is not in the forbidden list, so these
  fusions are already allowed to spill.

display_title: [XLA:PjRt] Add 512 bit transpose microkernels and runtime block sizing

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PjRt] Add 512 bit transpose microkernels and runtime block sizing

`TransposePlan` previously capped vectorized inner blocks at 16 or 32 bytes at
compile time and lacked 512 bit Highway transpose kernels. Partial remainder
tiles also fell directly back to scalar element copies.

Add spill free 512 bit transpose microkernels in `xla/pjrt/transpose_kernels.cc`
covering 64 byte, 32 byte, and 16 byte rows with sequential row stores. Select
square, half, or strip kernels by target and stride alignment to avoid L1D set
thrashing. Keep Zen 4 narrow element blocks within 256 bit halves to avoid
double pumped cross lane permutes. Select the inner block byte limit from the
active Highway target at runtime, leaving 16 byte elements at scalar block size.
Recursively halve partial remainder tiles into smaller power of two SIMD blocks
down to 16 byte rows. Existing transpose outputs are bit identical and no flags
are added.
